title: A completely smooth move, for which we probably paid more than necessary
review: The 'move' (it was not a complete house move, just a shifting of some belongings from my late parents' place) went completely smoothly in every respect. Five stars for that.However, due largely to inexperience, we had booked much too large a van (we filled less than a quarter of the space), two men where maybe only one was really needed, and probably twice as much of their time as was necessary anyway. I am not certain how much needless cost this entailed, because the pricing structure is quite opaque, but my hunch is that we probably paid something like twice as much as we need have.When booking all this, I did explain to someone I now believe was the proprietor roughly what we expected to need to move. He did not even suggest that I might have been over-ordering. I think it might have been useful if he had at least mentioned the possibility.Anyway, better to have too much room etc than too little, I suppose!PS.   Finest Van telephoned me to discuss my concerns. They gave me a very modest refund, which I took as a welcome gesture of goodwill, although it made no real difference to the economics. They are good to deal with, though, and, having learned my lesson, I would be content to use them again if the need arose.

title: I got convinced to get the £80 Membership...
review: UPDATE: I have updated the rating from 1 star to 4 stars because their customer service team responded within days to this rating and refunded me the £80 without any argument. Further, the original cleaning job was always good (as mentioned in my original review). I got convinced to get the £80 per annum "membership". I received £30 off from an end of tenancy cleaning. In retrospect they overcharged me slightly even with the discount. However, the cleaning job was good. Fast forward a few months later. I asked for a quote on a move in cleaning, a quote on an oven cleaning, an electrician quote, and a quote on a garden/fance repair job (different time periods). The company was consistently way way above and competitor and when I indicated I would not go with them they immediately offered a 30-50% discount. Even so, they were STILL 10-20% above any other competitive quotes. Fast forward 11 months...they charged me for another £89 as they have an automatic renewal (that they do not tell you about during the phone call where they pressure you to sign up to that annual membership). The renewal apparently is charged our 1 month before the 12 months expiration!! In my view this is borderline to a scam and the membership is utterly worthless. Get them on a job by job basis and do NOT agree to the first price they give you when they call you first. A bit of a Turkish bazaar mentality this company.....

I'm very satisfied with the quality of the service provided.Previous review: Extremely likely this company is fraudulent due to their sketchy business practices.I signed up to their membership because of a promotional deal and booked two services to begin with. Be warned - they charge you in advance for a service you might not be happy with, it's seemingly impossible to get a refund and they charge the card you have on file for fees that are not pre-authorised. If you expect a job to be completed between 12pm - 1pm, they believe they have every right to show up at 12:58pm because that's the 'arrival time'. If you try and call them, you're left in a loop of automated messages. If you try and amend a service through your online dashboard, there's no confirmation of your request. title: Hit and miss but generally good
review: I think they are great when it comes to small jobs like cleaning and moving. I've used them a couple times for those services and have 0 complaints, the service has always been great and the staff were very efficient, friendly and professional. I took a risk and used them for a big job, to do the flooring in my hallway, which cost £655, I had to buy the flooring, underlay and trim separately, which was £258 so the service was £913 in total. The floorboards were laid okay but the finish was shocking and I'm unbelievably disappointed with the finished product and refuse to believe the worker is a professional. Without going into too much detail, he nailed and glued loose pieces of wood together for the trim and didn't cut them properly so some are sticking out overhanging the wall. The transition strips, don't cover the metal strip between the rooms. He was an hour late, didn't finish and had to come back another day then was 2 hours late. I had floor spacers from a previous job and he took them up and kept them all. I didn't realise he had stolen them until afterwards. He didn't take the waste with him so 2 weeks later I'm still trying to get rid of the wood.After complaining they gave me a refund of £115 for the service and £46 of for the additional materials that he asked me to buy didn't use. After the refunds, I spent £752 in total but I will need to remove the trim and transition strips and have it corrected.My honest opinion on Fantastic Services would be they are fantastic for small jobs like cleaning or tasks under £100. They are responsive and helpful with complaints and I appreciate they do what they can to make good when things don't go well.However, because their workers are contractors and sole traders, the person who is actually assigned to do your work could be terrible and so to me it isn't worth the risk if you're having to part with a significant amount of money. I wish I hadn't used them for my flooring but I will continue to use them for cleaning and odd jobs.Also, a point to note: If you pay for the yearly membership you get £300 credit. The credit works by deducting £30 from each purchase. So if you have £300 credit and buy a service for £200, you will still pay £170 and it will deduct £30 from your credit. Just FYI if you're planning on signing up.

title: Not so Fantastic...
review: Not so Fantastic...Once they get you as a customer if something goes wrong, expect it to be dealt with inefficiently.Unfortunately I had a terrible experience. I was convinced to join Fantastic Club as I booked for an End of Tenancy clean (EOT) to move into a new property (which was already a stressful situation).This cost me £313 with a FC discount. A lot of money for an EOT clean but the cheapest quote I got out of 4. They say you pay for what you get... and yes, it was certainly poor.My experience was that the cleaners did not meet general expectations of what FS promoted in terms of there End of Tenancy cleaning service (this was a move-in clean for me). The cleaners did not do a full oven, dishwasher, washine machine and fridge clean. Skirtings were full of dust and hair, and the toilet showed dirt around. I took several photos moments after the cleaners left to demonstrate the poor cleaning job. The cleaners caused damage in my bathroom (a leak appeared out of nowhere and I was not immediately informed. I Unfortunately found this and cleaners were quick to tell me it was a leak before they rushed out the door). I called FS 10mins after the cleaners rushed out the door and they re-booked me a re-clean for 4days later. The re-clean was CANCELLED BY FS 20mins before it was due to happen in the evening, at my inconvenience. FS informed me via messaging rather than a phone call, but did not fully explain the cancellation at short notice. They did not call me to re-book this in. Poor customer service after they make a sale. I was huegly let down. Due to proximity to Xmas and my removals arriving, I had to source a local cleaner who was far cheaper yet did a better job than FS - she was not leaving until I was absolutely happy with the oven, dishwasher and washine machine. It was a week battle with FS customer service to get a partial refund after providing many images, another cleaners invoice and constantly calling and messaging. They are quick to get the sale, but very slow when you have a problem. In terms of the leak, they are sending out the plumber with a caveat that "if the plumber finds the leak is nothing to do with the cleaners, I will get charged". They already made claims my leak was not caused by the cleaners, despite them not being the ones staying in the property to know when the leak appeared! This is not booked in for another week and a half. So the bucket I bought will keep catching the water until then...It couldnt get worse that this! Oh but it did... then just hours after Christmas day I recieved an email from the head of customer services saying I'm going to be "charged for cancelling a service 48hrs before it was due to take place". I had not cancelled nor booked any more services after the horrific experience I have had so far. The plumber is what they are looking to send out in the New Year! I refused to book any more services with FS. It has been an absolute nightmare over what is a most stressful period of moving home a week before Christmas! After back and forth negotiation via messaging for a week, the partial refund I got on Xmas day was going to be the reason I did not write a bad review, but it was an email hours later from their Head of Customer Service claiming I will be charged for cancelling a service I didn't even book, was the last straw for me!! It was Greystar (huge global property developer) who recommended FS through their residents app, if Greystar wants to continue with their high standards, then FS should not be their recommended service company. Well, I will now be writing to Greystar... I am hugely disappointed.

title: A Very Poor Cleaning Service
review: Booked for 1pm and after booking I received a confirmation of my booking with arrival of 1.00-2.30pm. They should mention before you pay that the time you book for is not necessarily the time they will come. It was not a problem for me personally but I imagine it would be for many busy people.The property was empty and had had a deep clean only two weeks previously when the tenants moved out. This was just for a general clean to spruce it up a bit for the new tenants. I had written on my booking that the main focus of the cleaning was the kitchen. I asked the cleaner to wash the glasses and kitchen utensils and wipe out the kitchen cupboards. I had booked for three hours cleaning and after two hours the cleaner called to say she had finished ( I do not have a problem with cleaners finishing early if the do the job quickly). When I went to the property, the glasses had been washed and left to dry in the rack but all the other utensils were still sitting on the worktop untouched, where I had left them for her. Nothing else in the kitchen had been cleaned (worktop, sink, cupboards, microwave, floor, etc.).Other than the two bathrooms, the rest of the property looked untouched. Even the cleaning products I had bought and placed on the coffee table were still in the exact same place.A very disappointing service and I am afraid I could not recommend Fantastic Services at all for their cleaning. There are much better cleaning companies out there.

title: I booked a deep clean for 4pm and…
review: I booked a deep clean for 4pm and nobody turned up or contacted me. I rang the number many times but just got an automated reply saying that I would be contacted in due course. Eventually, at 6.10pm, over two hours later, a member of the original sales team rang to check up on me. Apparently the company tried to call me twice - once at at 5.32pm, and once more after that (one and a half hours after the original time slot). I received a text at 5.36pm apologising and saying that the service would need to be rescheduled. I felt very surprised and disappointed that nobody contacted me before this to tell me that the cleaner would not be attending. I would have expected at the very least to be told promptly that my cleaner was late/not attending, rather than wait around for a long time with no information. I had been assured by the sales team that cleaners arrived promptly with this company and that customer service was a strength. However,  I was waiting around at home for a long time with no information. I also followed the company’s instructions about how to get information about where my cleaner was but there was no way to get that information or evidence of my bookings on the website. On the eventual phone call, at 6.10pm - which lasted for about 45 minutes - I asked for compensation they offered me a sum of 10% off of the deep clean total of £110. I said I felt this was insufficient and they offered me £20 maximum. I had to change all my plans for the evening and had to cancel what I was going to originally do. I lost a lot of time organising, chasing this up, waiting around, and then making follow up calls. Eventually, just before 7pm, I finished my phone call with the company in which they agreed to process a refund and cancellation. I received an email then confirming this, but informing me that I would also need to speak to membership services for that particular part of the refund too and have since received an email saying my membership has been confirmed, so I have more following up to do still about ensuring this is actually cancelled.

title: DO NOT ACCEPT THE GOVERNMENT GRANT…
review: DO NOT ACCEPT THE GOVERNMENT GRANT SCHEME THROUGH 0800 REPAIR.I was told about the "free" replacement boiler service through 0800 repair. After months of back and forth, I was eventually approved for getting a new boiler as well as other additions to my home.I was advised that the only cost to me, was that the engineers would have to bring up the stairs and bedroom carpet and these would need to be replaced. To which I agreed.What I was left with was nothing short of absolutely shocking.I informed via phone call before the work took place that my gas fire was to be capped off, and I would need a gas engineer to turn it back on. I agreed.My fire was then removed, dumped in my front garden filled with cigarette ends from the workmen. Which I then had to dispose of myself.I was told that the boiler would be put on the flush wall where a cupboard used to be in my 7 year olds room, it was not. It was an absolute mess. I have since had to pay out over £400 to resolve this.I was left with a fan in one bathroom without a cover. And another fan that was not able to be connected unless I wanted trunking around the walls of my bathroom. I was left with brown marks on the ceiling of my kitchen under where the boiler is upstairs. Additionally, for the next few weeks after the installation, I had brown streaks running down my kitchen window every time it rained.I gave 0800 Repair a chance to resolve this and sent them photos of the issues. A manager came over to assess. Provided me with some paint for the marks on the kitchen ceiling. #Said he would get a new cover for the fan.Advised that there is some additional pipe work that needs put together at the rear of the building (which I have since been informed from a local tradesperson, is actually dangerous to be left the way it is).Told me that he couldn't do anything about a new fire, however when they come back to look at the repairs, woudl drill a hole in the wall to get a plug through for an electric fire. This was 3 months ago, I have heard nothing since.A few weeks ago, I rang to follow this up and gave the name of the manager who came out. I was told that this would be followed up. Still nothing.This work got done 3 months ago, the area where the boiler is is still not complete. I still have awful leftovers from the work that has been done. I am currently seeing absolutely no benefits to the new boiler price-wise. So if you are reading this and its anything to do with the "free" boiler replacement. Don't do it, you will absolutely regret it. An absolute joke of a company.

title: A little more considerationwhen working in someones home
review: I requested a visit to fit a fused spur to accommodate a sump pump. When the engineer arrived he thought he was coming to fit an outside light and was unable to do the job requested. A little more care would have been appreciated when it is known you will be working inside someones home.UPDATEThank you for your response Kev and also for the email you sent me. I did not reply to this email as I did not wish to get into an argument with you. However, as you have chosen to bring a response to Trust Pilot I must reply as follows.:-Your firm did an enormous amount of work for me last year and because I was impressed with how Peter Cannon and the trainee conducted themselves,  I came back to you. You may also find I did give you a 5* review following this work.I can categorically confirm your lads did not work in their stockinged feet, they also had to go into the kitchen to look at the fuse box housed in a kitchen cupboard. Consequently, the mud, dirt, from their boots trod into my carpet in the doorway and also into the kitchen. Had I been made aware they had dirty shoes I could have provided floor covering.I was also extremely surprised when you personally initially turned up to do the job (fitting a fused spur) thinking you had come to do something to a light? I had filled in your on line form giving full details of my requirements and also mentioned these again when I spoke to you on the telephone. You personally were unable to undertake the job when you came, due to ill health, therefore delaying this job until you had someone available, the day before the sump pump was fitted. Had there been a problem it could have been extremely inconvenient.

title: Disappointing LVT
review: *I have tried to upload photos but Tile Mountain have turned off this option* We purchased the Watson almond luxury vinyl flooring in November 2022, it has been down less than two years and has been a real disappointment. title: Possibly the worst customer service…
review: Possibly the worst customer service I’ve experienced in a long time. I ordered over £1,000 worth of tiles for a project. Completing the work myself, I ended up being 9 tiles short. Understanding that batch variations happen, especially over time, I placed an additional order, expecting minor differences. Instead, the tiles delivered were undersized by 5mm—a significant deviation from nominal size and well outside the British Standards tolerances.When I contacted customer service, what should have been a straightforward request to swap the tiles turned into a drawn-out and frustrating ordeal. Despite providing photographs, measurements, and official British Standards documentation proving the tiles were out of tolerance, Tile Mountain repeatedly insisted the tiles were within limits, citing batch variations as the cause. They refused to acknowledge the issue or accept fault. Even at resolution, it was clear they weren’t trying to help but were instead focused on getting rid of me.Adding to the frustration, my case was handled by different customer service representatives at various stages, leading to conflicting messages and further delays. For example, I was initially offered a swap for a closer batch, only to be told later that a swap wasn’t possible. After much persistence, they claimed to have found a matching batch—only to later inform me that they couldn’t locate it after all. I was then told to wait another month for the next available batch. Ultimately, they found a batch matching the correct caliber 5 size and arranged delivery, though they cautioned there might be slight color variations—a compromise I was willing to accept. Finally, when the replacements arrived, they were caliber 4, leaving them mismatched in size once again.I’ve decided to use the tiles as-is because I cannot face another two months of being dismissed and gaslit by a company that refuses to accept responsibility for clear errors, even when presented with indisputable evidence. Tile Mountain’s inability to provide basic customer service, compounded by inconsistent communication between their team members, has been nothing short of exhausting. I would strongly advise anyone considering this company to look elsewhere if they value their time and peace of mind.

review: The transfer to InterfaceNRM was well organised and well managed.Timing was correct and the transition was a positive experience. The sales management, operations management, scheme management from Interface was, and continues to be, excellent.Clear, concise, cooperative and easy to understand.However when the time came to audit I was less than positively impressed. My principal concern was that when asked a question during the audit, I frequently couldn't finish/complete my answer due to continuous interruptions or statements from the auditor. At one point the InterfaceNRM auditor asked why they hadn't received a particular document/report. My answer was simply that they hadn't asked for it.In another example I was asked/told that I should collate approx 70 specific spreadsheet reports. I disagreed. I was then pointedly asked......"why not?" My reply was that it wasn't a requirement of the standard. The auditor's loss of words that followed.....anyway we eventually struggled through.The subsequent audit report arrived around 9 weeks later and was quite vague in parts.

QCS is the leading digital provider of compliance management, policies, and procedures that are always up to date enabling over 5,000 social care organisations to deliver and evidence the highest quality care. At its core is QCS Compliance Management System - your digital hub for quality compliance and knowledge. We make compliance management easy so you can focus on what matters most – delivering quality care. With policies, procedures, and compliance toolkits shaped to your business, you can be safe in the knowledge with QCS Policy Centre your business will always be up to date with any changes to legislation, regulation, and best practice whatever happens. From guidance on care planning to business operations, medications management to human resources, and up-to-date guidance on the latest regulatory requirements, QCS Resource Centre gives you easy access to the latest best practice guidance and resources for delivering quality care. Driven by evidence-based tools and practical guidance on how to deliver quality dementia care, QCS Dementia Centre helps transform the assessment, management, and evidencing of care provision for those living with dementia. All of this is supported by QCS App, giving you access anywhere, anytime, and on any device – 24/7.

title: Expensive, but no other option !!
review: QCS was efficient in the initial setup. £1800 saw me get the 3 huge files filled with every policy and procedure you can think of. As a very small dom care agency it would have been almost impossible to write these before our first inspection, so for that we are grateful. However having worked with the documents for over a year and are now paying £149 per month, I am not too convinced it represents value for money. Nearly all policies have needed editing by myself as they are very geared towards care/residential homes. We have scrapped thier assessment forms altogether and have cobbled one up ourselves. Our service users hated the questions we were asking and the forms were very invasive, way beyond CQC outcomes for needs assessments in dom care. I do like the principle behind the organisation and the updates now sent as hard copies in the post, but I will be seriously considering not bothering at all next year unless I start to see the support I thought I was paying for in the field in which my company specialises. Generic anything is no good to me. I thought I was paying for tailor made????

title: QCS: The Website That Never Fails to Amuse
review: I must admit, this website ranks among the worst I've ever encountered, and I say this with complete honesty. It not only wastes your time but also your money.The most frustrating aspect revolves around the conspicuous absence of functionality when it comes to administrative tasks. If you need to make changes to user accounts, there's no user-friendly interface available. Instead, you're left with no choice but to get in touch with their support team and patiently await their manual adjustments, which, regrettably, can consume a significant amount of time. To illustrate, if you're dealing with ten different locations under your QCS, and an employee needs to transfer from one location to another, you're in for a challenging process. You'll need to submit a support ticket and brace yourself for the update, and here's the frustration—it only occurs on Fridays (the transfers in our company). So, prepare to wait another three days to get it resolved. It's quite a vexing ordeal.Moreover, extracting data from the site is virtually impossible. It resembles a basic, rudimentary platform that even an entry-level full-stack developer could create. However, it falls short in providing essential features like report extraction and a properly functioning admin backend site. Were left with going into every single user profile to check their progress (becomes frustrating when you have more than 200 employees and 2 member team responsible to do reporting's on qcs)But what genuinely leaves me perplexed is the user account setup. If an email address is already linked to another company's QCS, you'll find yourself unable to add it to your tenant for account creation. Instead, you're compelled to follow a convoluted process of sending a formal email request and enduring what seems like an eternity—approximately 4-5 hours—for them to address the issue.In summary, my experience with this website has been an immense waste of time and a continuous source of deep frustration. I strongly recommend exploring alternatives that offer a more efficient and user-friendly platform.

title: Very satisfied
review: After a few weeks of research we chose 1st Move (who were not the cheapest) but appeared to offer everything we required. I read some reviews which were both good and bad. (The bad made me wonder if we’d chose the right company to move our belongings) I can honestly say that whenever I had a query/question Tessa answered immediately. All staff that I had contact with were above and beyond helpful. We couldn’t fault the professionalism of the staff, even those that came to the house under Covid times. We packed the majority of items ourselves and left anything of value that required insuring to 1st move. Upon receiving our freight in Austin TX it was well packed, well sealed. Not a drop of moisture was visible anywhere. No items were damaged.The US delivery company were indeed 1 man, so expect when it states curb side drop off, that’s exactly what you get unless there is an option to get them to unload within your property.The only niggles I have is the small print really requires reading by everyone at the start of the process and familiarise yourself several weeks later, 4-6 week delivery was quoted, but that was a little on the optimistic side. I guess with all the world issues currently, it took 9 weeks door to door (but Covid is the new normal now and so this should always be factored in)Watch out for little hidden charges at the destination delivery. Further taxes to pay. (Less than $100 but just a reminder that it’s in the small print)Overall very satisfied and would recommend 1st Move to anyone and I’d certainly use them again if required.

title: Mixed bag
review: The good: My shipment from the UK arrived on Vancouver Island with no losses or damages. The sales rep, the transport manager, and the team who came to collect my shipment were all helpful and personable.The not ideal, but acceptable: My shipment was delivered almost nine weeks after collection, longer than communicated but not terrible in the scheme of things.The bad: Communication from the Move Coordination team representative ranged from highly confusing to dangerously incorrect. I was misadvised on customs documentation, and was glad that I had done my own research and took documentation I was explicitly told by 1st Move that I didn't need. Insurance offered was pretty poor, but probably not worse than industry standard given the lack of options. Essentially, if you opt for anything but basic coverage, everything you want covering for loss is charged at the higher coverage rate, but only those items which are professionally packed by 1st Move are covered for damage or theft. Anything self-packed that is to be covered for loss is still charged at the same higher rate even though it's not covered at the higher level ie for damage/theft. Communication from the move coordination team rep on professional packing and what would be charged was pretty terrible and outright contradicted by the team who actually came to collect my shipment. The volume of my goods ended up probably 25% bigger when wrapped in all of 1st Move's bubble wrap. I understand why the packing materials are necessary, but worth bearing in mind when budgeting for a move.Communication from the Canadian agent arranged by 1st Move was pretty minimal despite specific questions which should have been easily answerable (such as the location of the customs office for clearance in Vancouver - I am sure this is not new and doesn't change). No accommodation made for my requirements or personal circumstances, and storage and detention charges were raised unnecessarily which created additional stress. Honestly not a pleasant experience dealing with this team, and not a good reflection on 1st Move who subcontracted them.Overall the experience was made a lot more stressful and complicated than it needed to be or than it easily could have been, but my shipment did arrive safely in the end.

title: Misleading conversations and documentation and poor value.
review: I recently moved from the UK to Australia.The staff were friendly but not entirely on t he ball. I asked for my delivery to be door to door. That was the conversation I had on  the phone. Turns out that's not what was on the quote. The quote only said the City. I missed that bu tr assumed the ongoing conversation had made that clear. I provided an address and that's where I assumed my goods would go.The company charged far above other providers, and it probably cost some 30-40% more in the end after clearance costs in australia. They may have been quicker getting it on a ship, but they took an extra 2-3 weeks to get me my paperwork to allow the goods to be shipped. They provided no guidance as to what the duties, charges or clearance costs may have been at trhe port o ff entry. A company in this business should be able to provide a guide. It could have been a million bucks for all I knew (be in g facetious). Conversations on trhe phone suggested these costs were included in the price, although the quote does Cleary state they are not. I was told verbally this would be covered.I may be at fault for not understanding or missing the fine print, but the guys on t he phone did nothing to make it clear.My quotation also increased after I had supplied t he goods. I shipped less goods with another company previously and was quoted less volume by over 1 cubic metres. They also charge a minimum of 2 cubic metres. I estimated the volume of my goods and think their estimate may be pushing boundaries. I don't want to pay for extra volume because of inefficient packing on their part. It was a significant increase on the initial quote. I would advise to avoid these guys and stick with one of the other established players such as Allied Pickfords. They may take marginally longer, but they are far more transparent and will work out better value...significantly better based on experience.

title: 1st Move International were very responsive.
review: 1st Move International were very friendly and seemingly upfront with their business. The Shipping was fast (but see below comments), the packing was efficient and friendly. They responded to queries quickly and were always available on the phone or email. I felt they were good to deal with. There was a breakdown of information and therefore expectations when out shipment arrived in Australia:TRUST being the point of this review- I have deducted two stars for the following reasons where my trust has wavered:-The delivery time was not accurate, as was commented by the agents when our shipment arrived into the landing port... 1st Move International advised 1 day transfer to the final depot point (in a different state to the landing port) but this was wildly inaccurate. It took an extra 10 days to arrive. The agents did explain that they have previously told 1st Move International, but commented ‘They have No idea and don’t seem to be bothered finding out’.-I lost some trust when the 1st Move Staff were dismissive of Australian Quarantine declaration. I queried items and they said not bother declaring, but I knew full well that this was totally incorrect advice.-there was disclaimers about paying the cost of Port fees not included - but the amount was not individualised for our destination which would have been helpful information. A point that I appreciate is out of 1st Move International’s control is the length of time Australian Quarantine takes to clear effects- I am still waiting after 5 weeks of the shipment arriving in Australia for Quarantine to process the paperwork, inspect and release the shipping for us to finally start our life. I am questioning whether it was worth paying more for fast shipping if it is all going to take so long anyways.

title: Started okay but went downhill and became expensive
review: Pick up was fine. Due to a lengthy visa delay I had to store my shipping pallet with 1st Move International and it was expensive. They duly charged me for more storage. I have just found out that my things have arrived at the destination that day after I left, which means I'll have to pay maximum storage costs there too. This is only due to 1st Move's wrong advice - had I stayed with the original date I would have saved a lot of money (c.£400) and had my things sooner. I've written to them to ask them to pay for the additional storage cost - I'm almost certain they won't even though they're essentially responsible for it. Also, another person mentioned the subcontractors in the destination country - expect lots of additional costs at that end.

title: mild form of extortion
review: The people we dealt with were all very good and the packers did an excellent job. The fluidity of the move was 5 stars, but lack of upfront clarity is not good enough in this business.We were quoted a price (granted with a footnote about costs not included on the other side, non-UK, of the shipment). This price was higher than the rest, but the service offer promised seemed to be worth the extra price tag. Then after collection and the shipment setting sail we get a note that the shipment is due to arrive in Cape Town (our destination) and that an extra payment is due, as expected.However, the scale of the payment came as a surprise. Essentially adding 50% of the total cost, we had budgeted for. While a footnote (As mentioned above) points this out, I believe it is the duty of the sales people to help the non-merchant understand what costs lie ahead. After paying £2,000 and then receiving a bill for another £1,000 while my possessions are being "held captive" on-board a ship, is a mild form of extortion. I can hardly ask the ship to turn around at this point, so I am stuck having to pay a sizeable amount that I was not aware of.I don't see how it can be difficult for an estimate to be provided to clients, rather than the support staff just saying "you had the footnote on the contract". That is not good enough if the footnote accounts for 33% of the total cost. The support staff asked me if I had not seen the footnote and I commented that this is not my profession and I am paying them a lot of money as professionals in the industry to help me understand what is coming my way. 1st Move International failed to meet a professional conduct standard and as such I would not suggest anyone to use their service.

title: Shipping Goods from UK to Canada When My Mum Died
review: My mum died in April, and I shipped some sentimental items from the UK to Canada using 1st Move International.  On the UK side they were very good - They came to the house and packed the items very well.1. First issue was when it came to insurance - I chose the most basic level, and 1st Move International came back and recommended that I increase the level of insurance.  I explained that it was impossible to replace items like photo albums, and the things I was shipping were only important to me because they were owned by my mum and dad.  To speed things up, I agreed to increase the level of insurance.  They then came back and told me the lowest amount I could insure for was 1,000 GBP, so I had to go through and put fake values on items that couldn't be replaced.2.  The agent on the Canadian side was COMPLETELY USELESS.  He contacted me using the wrong email address, so I only had two days to pick up the goods before I had to start paying storage at the warehouse. 3.  The agent told me that it was very quick and would only take a few minutes to clear the goods through customs, omitting to let me know that there is at least a 1.5 hour queue. This was important because I got to the agent's office later than planned.4.  I had to call at the agent's office to pay them in cash, and when I got to the warehouse about 20 mins later he had not released the shipment, so I had to wait.  The agent had sent the release earlier in the day, but it has expired because I was delayed.5. The agent didn't let me know that you aren't allowed to break down the shipment to load it at the warehouse, and that I would need to ensure I rented a large enough truck.6.  Experience on the Canadian side was HORRIBLE.  Not only would I not use 1st Move International again, but I wouldn't ship anything internationally again because it was so bad.

title: Helpful at first but poor packing and directors that ignore you don't make for a good experience.
review: Incredibly helpful, up until something goes wrong. We had our stuff collected from our storage unit in the UK to be taken to their depot for re-packing and checking before shipping to the US in a container. This bit went well, they where helpful on the phone and the team who came to collect stuff were quick and efficient. Once it had made it over we asked if it was possible to redirect it, which they then spent a week working out they couldn't for a reasonable price (racking us up a $700 demurage charge) rather than just telling us straight away as we had a plan in place if they couldn't. When we finally received our stuff we discovered they had not bothered to re-pack nearly anything we had asked (and paid!) them for including my mountain bike which was declared on the insurance, and so had to be packed by them to be insured. Also we found that having told them multiple times that the plastic boxes our stuff was packed in could not be stacked too high or the lids collapse, that for most of the pallets they were stacked high, and then had heavy things thrown on top, including 25Kg odd of diving lead! My heavy metal tool cabinets were stuck on the top of high stacks with no protection to stop them rubbing against each other, while boxes of computer monitors were put at the bottom, so they were supporting the weight of everything above. Out of the 9 pallets in the container, only one was stacked how they said they would, and this was the only one with undamaged boxes.  If you watch the packing videos on their website, You're pretty much going to get the opposite. When we complained we had an email from the director saying they would get back to us, then nothing, despite several follow up emails.  In short, very helpful and friendly until you open the container and realize that they've done a half-hearted and slapdash job of packing, and you're now picking bits of broken plastic box out of everything...

title: Good local team- poor communication and unknown additional costs once shipped.
review: My experience with 1st Move International is very similar to that described by other reviewers which I had read prior to selecting the company. In summary, the local team and packing were great, but as it's likely you will need to deal with an unknown agent, customs, quarantine, port handling, personal collection and transportation (or arrange another company to do so), I would question whether a door to door service is actually cheaper than the appealing low quote you will receive from 1st Move International for their service, and undoubtedly easier in the long run. Prior to committing to the shipment the sales representative was responsive, helpful and communication was good. On collection day the local team were efficient, friendly and careful. I believe my boxes and other goods were pack on a palate and bubble wrapped relatively efficiently, with the overall volume only slightly more than I would have expected. Once shipped though, 1st Move International's involvement is more or less complete, and you will from then onwards be dealing with local agents who take care of shipping, port handling, customs and quarantine, unloading and collection. Minimal details are given by 1st Move International on how to negotiate this part of the delivery, and while each agent will undoubtedly vary, I was provided minimal details. Add to this unknown terminology and procedures and you may find this all pretty annoying and confusing. You then need to be expecting to pay additional costs, all which are unknown in advance. The purpose of some of these costs are still unclear to me even after detailed discussion with the agent. If you expect these costs and aren't concerned with additional $500 then it's ok. But ultimately, this is where you need to really consider whether your decision to go with 1st Move International is correct. In terms of time for transportation, my goods were collected, wrapped and on the ship after 12 days. The overall shipping time from UK to Sydney was estimated to be 6 weeks, but was 7 weeks. So overall, delivery from UK to Sydney took ~9 weeks.  Regarding packaging and safe transit of goods, all my items were received without damage. As quarantine inspected my package some parcels were left partially opened, which could have resulted in some exposure to rain etc, particularly if I hadn't collected promptly. In summary- you know what you are getting in to by going with 1st Move International. It may work out cheaper for you, but it may not be worth your time to make such a small saving.

title: At first everything was wonderful... in the UK... and then my belongings arrived in the US
review: The process of setting up, understanding customs, pricing, etc. was wonderful - they were human, pleasant, coordinated, friendly, and really a breath of fresh air to someone who has done several international relocations.  They explained everything patiently, even several times when we got confused.  Our account manager was easy to reach, knew our situation personally, and was a real pleasure.  The drivers who arrived on the day of the move were friendly, fun, inspired confidence, and weren't joking around, though they were regular guys.  All in all, when my belongings left London in a van I was very impressed.  I was kept in touch with exact timetables.  The pictures of our stuff on their facebook page inspired confidence.  Great customer service all around.Then the nightmare started.  My belongings were passed to a US agent who didn't know anything.  Alyssa at DGS logistics appeared out of the blue, didn't introduce herself and just sent us a bill, and our contact with this US partner firm was worse than useless, contradicting herself many times, not seeming to know what was going on, being abrupt and borderline rude, not informing us of the obvious.  We had (per the suggestion of 1st move) not paid for the US delivery at origin.  There were all kinds of fees attached in a completely opaque way, and the charges and timeline changed several times.  When we asked to have our belongings delivered to our house, we were told that interior delivery was not an option and they would leave the shirnk wrapped pallet outside of our home.  Both my wife and I travel for work, so with no assurance exactly when it would arrive we couldn't take that option.  So we were told the only other option was to go to the local freight terminal and pick it up ourselves.  This is a place where only truckers seem to go - no other civilians.  Several of the staff were lovely, but many were outright rude at our not knowing how things worked.  We had to go get a box cutter and break down our pallet ourselves, load into our cars, they wouldn't let us leave a partial load since our cars wouldn't fit everything, it was an absolute nightmare - plus we had to carry our belongings like the movers we thought we'd paid for.  I injured my back carrying boxes like a college student, we lost a day of work each, and we had an awful time at arrival.  This went from being an extremely buttoned up service.So here's my suggestion - if you're going to use these guys, make sure that (a) you've paid for an exact level of service you want all the way to your home, and that 1st move is going to be accountable for the progress of your goods through to your door - do not accept that you will have to deal with anyone else; just make them deal with it and keep your account manager at 1st move as your only point of contact, and (b) articulate contractually exactly what is being provided - including the breakdown of pallet and removal of debris.I loved this service for the first 3/4 of the experience - would have been 5 stars all the way; but the actual handover to the US and the delivery was below 1 star, completely unacceptable.  Don't go in with your eyes closed.  Maybe their partner in your part of your destination country will be better than ours was, but I wouldn't count on it.

title: Where to start… Book somewhere else
review: Where to start… They offer great customer service until they have packed your stuff and possess all the power over your stuff.The guys who came to pack our stuff on the moving day wasn’t aware that we had booked them to pack the stuff. They also pretended to send us links to review them on Tripadvisor, however we never received the links. Which is a massive red flag and explains why Tripadvisor have 4.5 stars, while Yelp has 1 star and Google have 3.8 stars. Very dodgy!The only positive part was that our stuff did arrive in a good condition which of course is a huge relief… But your belongings are better off with a different company, hence my one star.

title: Shipment seriously damaged and complete lack of customer service

title: Dont ship anything you can't replace with these people!
review: I was shipping items from my deceased mother's home in the Uk to my home in the USA. I was sending unique unreplaceable items of limited monetary value.  I sent the minimum purchase amount of 3 sqM, which i carefully worked out. The items were packed into just 2.08 sqM by 1st Move by placing heavy boxes on top of the one piece of furniture I shipped, my deceased father's chair. This caused two of the chair legs to be smashed off in transit due to the chair being placed on a thin piece of unsupported cardboard and having heavy weight items placed upon it. Other items were also smashed including a small cupboard made by my father, which also had very heavy items stacked on top of it. Multiple storage boxes had their lids smashed for the same reason. one of these had been taped up, which it was not when collected by 1st move, suggesting they broke it before they packed the pallet, which was sealed on arrival, and they just taped it over and threw it in the pallet anyway. I found a roll of plastic wrap and a discarded used/empty sellotape centre inside the pallet that were not mine. (attention to detail??) This follows poor communication, in which I had to repeat the same information to different people in the organisation. They send out generic emails, often with repeated sentences and typing errors. A number of emails I received appeared not to relate to my situation at all but were sent out because that is what they do. Staff members changed entries on my paperwork, without asking me, because they thought they knew better than me what I was shipping before they collected it. On the day of collection, they arrived hours late for the collection appointment. They sent me two emails asking me to write this review-how smart is that?A few pounds of insurance money will not make up for the damage these people have done, to maximise their profits. Please consider other shipping options, especially if you are shipping anything that cannot be replaced.

title: Little value for monoey
review: We booked a pest control service through Rentokil to help with a small but stubborn mouse problem. Although the cost seemed very steep to me - over £500 - I was assured from your reviews and reputation that the service would be worth the cost and eradicate our pest issue.Our exterminator Clare was helpful, responsive, prompt and efficient. However, it became clear on arrival for her first of three visits that her remit was to (1) lay traps and (2) offer fairly standard advice that we could have pulled off the internet ourselves (closing gaps and keeping food off floors etc.). Her second and third visits proceeded in the same way, with some shifting of the traps to different rooms and ensuring they were working. We caught one mouse but still had droppings, but after our three visits, our engagement was over - although she did try to convince us of the benefit of entering into a monthly contract.I fail to see how any of the service we were offered was different than if I had purchased and laid traps myself for a much smaller fee. After we finished our contract period, I could not help but feel like I had not gotten any value whatsoever for my money and had perhaps been misled into the impact our investment in the pest control process would have.While again, I want to praise the service we received from Clare, I will not be using Rentokil again or recommend them to anyone I know in need of exterminator service.

title: Shambolic service
review: I contacted Rentokil about a rodent problem. The representative visited the premisses, she sent through the proposal which needed some altering. This was done quickly and sent back. Payment was made and no information was forthcoming about the operative coming to put traps out. I had to email for information about the visit, I finally received a call. He returned after a week and said one mouse had been caught. He then said he'd be back in a couple of weeks. No appointments were made through regular lines of communication (email). I had to email again to find out what was happening and was informed that the final visit would be Friday and the traps would be removed then as well. We were charged £2,800 for around 3 weeks of contract and 3 visits, this has amounted to one mouse being caught and around 12 working hours. I think this is an extortionate amount of money for very little service in which I had to do most of the communication. In conclusion, I would not recommend this company and definitely know the service offered is not worth the extortionate cost.

Once we opened the box we found a large amount of our plates and bowls broken in tiny pieces, with none of them being protected with bubble wrap.When we contacted Buzz Catering, their customer service advisor Jo Elliott was extremely unhelpful, claiming we had to try and puzzle piece the broken bits together to then take pictures of every single broken plate or bowl for them to replace them. We tried to be honest with them and explained that we had some unbroken pieces, only to find out a few days later that there had been hairline cracks in a couple more that we hadn’t initially noticed. Jo wouldn’t give us a full refund (even though not one of the plates or bowls was bubble wrapped and no FRAGILE was anywhere to be found on the box) claiming it wasn’t their fault. Jo then said we could receive INDIVIDUAL replacements (for ONLY those reported broken in the first 24 hours, not the ones with cracks we hadn’t noticed til after) but these replacements wouldn’t arrive until at least February as the factory was closed. They suggested that we take a partial refund and then reorder a brand new set of plates and bowls, which would result in us paying even more money to them after their error.We were really excited to try Buzz Catering and were bitterly disappointed with our experience both with the delivery, and especially with customer services and Jo. We’re now going to take our partial refund and order from a different company.

title: Awful Customer Service - DO NOT ORDER FROM HERE!
review: Unfortunately I have nothing good to say about this company. I was excited to order from them as I assumed, being a catering company, it would all be great. I was very wrong! I ordered an entirely new set of crockery, 6 plates large, 6 small and 6 pasta bowls and 6 small bowls. They arrived completely shattered in pieces, I could only salvage maybe 2 of each item. I contacted them and they said that I had to photograph each individual broken item in order to get a replacement. I tried my best to do this but I made it very clear that this wasn't possible for every item as honestly some bits were in thousands of little pieces and I am sorry I didn't have the time to be playing puzzle time to get the photos for them. I (stupidly) assumed that their customer service would be very understanding and send out an entirely new order once again considering no fragile label or bubble wrap was used in the shipping whatsoever. But oh how I was wrong! I spoke with Jo Elliot who was very little help, they said that only replacement items would be sent but they wouldn't be available for three months. When I proceeded to say that we had found 3 more plates that we thought were fine but were actually covered in small hair line cracks on the base, we were told these wouldn't be replaced as they weren't informed in the first 24 hours!!! Good thing I was in when the shipment arrived completely broken because with my job I travel a lot and if I hadn't contacted them within 24 hours I wouldn't have even been offered a single replacement. What kind of customer service is that!?So after lots of back and forth, the only option Jo Elliot gave me was a partial refund of the broken items. So for an order where over 70% of the items were broken, I received 35% credit back. So I have basically just thrown £200 in the bin thanks to this company. I would not recommend to anyone and I think Jo Elliot should probably have a different job and not deal with customer service!

title: Is it worth the hype?
review: Is it worth the hype?Having recently seen the queues of the new King Street Manchester branch spilling out onto the street, I decided to pay a visit today to find out what the hype was about.  I left it until mid afternoon so I would avoid the queues and just wanted to grab a quick takeaway sandwich during my office lunch break.On entering I noticed the pre-made pot salads.  They looked lovely but were massively overpriced.  I couldn’t justify paying that much for such a small portion.  As I reached the counter a few things jumped out to me that I didn’t like. None of the food was covered, flies were buzzing around and landing on the food.  The counter display lacked something.  All the food was laid out on one level making it look overcrowded and unappealing.  Adding some risers would definitely improve the aesthetics here.The labels were partially hidden making it practically impossible to see the ingredients or prices.Customer Service :-Three times I had to tell the server that it was a takeaway and they still tried to serve it to me on a tray as a dine-in customer.  Such lack of attention to detail and really annoying. Not to mention I was probably charged dine-in prices! Definitely room for improvement.All that said, the food was really tasty. That I cannot fault. What I will say though is that it's too pricey and out of the acceptable range for a daily visit for my office lunch break.  I think with a slightly lower price point they would capture even more office trade.Verdict:  Great food but room for improvement in customer service and shop display.Would I visit again?  Probably.

title: Ridiculous overuse of biodegradable gloves
review: Every time I am in a Gail's bakery, I am just astonished and horrified by their overuse of biodegradable gloves. I then asked her if she would at least re-use these disposable gloves, but she said no she couldn't because they were now "contaminated" and had to go in the bin! I realise these gloves are biodegradable, but it still takes energy to make them, and they don't biodegrade so rapidly. Otherwise, I find their bread is nice, which is what I come in to buy. But I just find this overuse of gloves rather upsetting. Before Covid, these gloves were never used to this extent, and if someone touches a loaf of bread for one second or so, it's not going to make you ill! I just wonder how many of these gloves they get through a week ...

title: The Horse Is Hungry For A Reason
review: Firstly, I wanted to praise the staff. Not only were they friendly and very efficient, they also managed to keep a straight face when they brought out the food.Now, I know the Hungry Horse is the Ryanair of hospitality, and I was not expecting fine dining, but I did expect the food to be edible.I now know why it’s called the Hungry Horse. It’s because the horse would never go near the offerings, in this case from the festive menu (which incidentally was about as festive as my big toe).To add insult to injury we had a French man in our party who prides himself on his culinary abilities. Tragically he order the Brie and Cranberry bites as a starter. No salad as advertised. Just three sad little deep fried triangles slung on a plate with some cranberry sauce.The rest of the starters were acceptable - the soup, prawn cocktail and chicken strips were fine.Unfortunately, this was followed by the main course. The vegan members of our group were given Yorkshire puddings with their roast. In any ither situation this would have been a bonus because the remaining guests would have gladly fought over a spare yorky. Alas ladies and gents, this is no Toby. They tasted like a combination of wallpaper paste and flour, cooked in a hot oven for 30 minutes then kicked along a pavement before landing on your plate. The vegetables were so overcooked that it looked like a pile of slop and had zero flavour. The roast potatoes were OK.The Brussels sprouts with cheese was not cooked so I am not sure how it was ‘crisped under the grill’ . It had to go back but looked so revolting on its return we did not eat it.The absolute piece de resistance was the ‘turkey’. Never in my life have I been presented with such an abomination. I can genuinely say the slices of heavily processed poultry tasted, I kid you not, like you were eating the contents of a pig pen. I have no idea what was in it but Bernard Matthew’s would turn in his grave.Desserts were largely fine although my husband’s Christmas pudding would definitely be classed as a slither in our house.The warning signs were there. The restaurant was virtually empty, the bar service was slow and they were very short staffed.Either that or they were all running about catching the tumbleweed.I will sum this up and say that my husband never ever complains. He was going to speak to the staff on the way out because he was so astounded we could be charged for food that I would not offer as a booby prize to someone detained at His Majesty’s Pleasure.Being terribly British, and knowing that this sub par fayre is not the fault of the chap in charge of the microwave, we paid up and left.But Greene King, when the fat cats are sitting around the board table soon, planning Christmas 2025, desperately trying to increase profits, get them to mystery shop NOW so they have a chance to see what you are serving up.Yes, it was £20 a head. Yes, generally in life you get what you pay for, but it has to be palatable don’t you think?Greene King, Christmas is about making memories and this is something we as a family will never forget. So thank you for that.

title: Payroll normally goes OK but there are issues
review: Payroll normally goes OK, you get paid usually 2-3 weeks after the client has paid, minus the 50 odd percent tax of course.Setting up a private pension contribution takes forever, in my case about 6 months so I lost a significant contribution to my pension  and associated tax relief.They also have constraints around pensions in that you can't make a fixed contribution each month, neither can you make a lump sum contribution. Lots of red tape and explanations are needed to do anything in this area despite it being YOUR money. Expenses are a problem and not easy to get paid out.Think of Paystream as an agent for HMRC simply there to collect tax but offer you little support. They are your 'employer' only when it suits them - auto enrolling you in their pension scheme and trying to withold holiday pay etc.The madness of IR35 means you pay somebody to 'employ' you and treat you like a young child. Two stars for the payroll, very little else to recommend here other than the staff are friendly, if ineffective. I will be leaving (or should that be 'resigning') very soon...*****EDIT JAN 24******I have been in touch with a dedicated team leader who is helping to resolve issues discussed above and looking at ways to improve the immediate situation and evolve other aspects. Jack has been a great help, and clearly understands the situation. This gives me confidence that they are working to tighten up on the grumble areas, albeit within the inevitable limitations of the regulators. Bumped up to 3 stars, I feel a 4 is incoming...

title: So  many errors causing grief and checking
review: So  many errors causing grief and resulting in having to check up on these guys all the time. I'm not an accountant but have learnt a lot because of all the mistakes they've made... 1) incorrect VAT submitted - but when updated HMRC was still chasing for larger amount which cause no end of grief and letters from HMRC threatening action2) penalty from HMRC for above which I had to make a  case for Paystream to pay... ie they didn't offer any recompense for inconvenience caused and didn't offer to pay for penalty. It was small but it was the principle.3) incorrect advice about taking money out of company at end of tax year which resulted in £3000+ more in personal tax etc...and company tax4) when closing, incorrect advice about dividends to take out, which I checked and reconfirmed (my calculations were right). Hopefully the right amount was taken in the end.5) when closing, the paystream tax department didn't correctly inform payroll about additional salary week which resulted in issues when the final accounts were made (I had to pay it back )6) when closing, incorrect pension contribution amount suggested which I had to query. There was a 50% discrepancy between their suggestion and what I thought would be the contribution7) Final closing documents sent with request to sign and no discussion about the numbers. When I looked at the numbers they didn't match my bank account balance and surprisingly there was a loss declared, etc... this resulted in a full review of my accounts and quite a few discussions. In the end the books were balanced. 8) no real apologies for having to spend so much time checking up on them and correcting mistakes and no offer of recompense for such sloppy closing processes and advice. As far as I'm concerned, I've been doing most of the work. These are my complaints to date and the closing is not quite completed yet. title: No value for money!

At £150 a month, I ended up paying £1,800 over the course of a year, only to receive minimal service. All they ever did was produce an invoice for payment—something I could have easily done myself. When I decided to close my company, I was hit with a hefty additional bill, which added insult to injury.To make matters worse, they offered tax advice on how to distribute my dividend, information that I later found readily available online, for a shocking price of almost £800. This was an eye-opener for me—making money is incredibly hard, and I now see how much I wasted with this company. Looking back, I can only blame myself for trusting them.I joined them as a novice in business, and instead of offering support or guidance, I feel my lack of knowledge was exploited. I made it clear several times that I didn’t understand accounting, but no one cared to explain anything to me. At the end of the year, I was hit with a heavy tax bill that left everyone around me questioning the incompetence of this service.£150 a month for absolutely no value add. I will be swiftly moving elsewhere and strongly advise others to avoid this company unless you want to waste your hard-earned money.

I have fallen foul of the conditions numerous times and accepted it. Now, the conditions are so complex to follow and very finite that you must do things in a particular way. I recently used Quidco to book three different hotel stays with the same hotel change. All from the one Quidco link - I have done it that way before so couldn't see why this wouldn't have worked. Sadly not this time. I was told all my fault as I couldn't prove the link in the transaction. Strange as the first transaction logged, the 2nd and 3rd were visible at the same time and I was able to log the claim against the two immediately following the first, yet for some reason 'the transaction could not be proven'. Again, clearly my fault, I should have deleted the cookies before I made the transaction (even though the transaction showed on the account - and never had to do this before). Glad to know, that something I have done successfully many times is, on this occasion, my fault - especially as the offer for the hotel chain was on a 'bonus' transaction offer and the lowest cashback value which wasn't on offer out of the three was successful, but the two with higher than usual offers were not successful.

description: Holidaycottages.co.uk - Personally inspected Holiday Cottages for you across England, Wales and Scotland. Voted 'Gold' for customer service by Feefo.

review: Dashwood, Holtby, Yorkshire. This is a lovely, cosy and well equipped cottage, dog friendly and tucked away behind the main house in a quiet village. Well placed for visiting York as well as the surrounding area. We spent Xmas week here, (6 nights) enjoying the homemade Xmas cake as well as the   bread, milk and other essentials thoughtfully left by Michelle, the owner.  We’ve stayed in quite a few cottages with various providers and this certainly ranks very high on the list.  Would happily return.

description: Holidaycottages.co.uk - Personally inspected Holiday Cottages for you across England, Wales and Scotland. Voted 'Gold' for customer service by Feefo.

review: Beautiful, huge chapel suitable for up to 8 people (plus dog). Three large bedrooms with en-suites, plus one twin with shower room on level below.Great walks to the local beach and beyond. Ten mins drive to Barmouth or Harlech. Host kept in touch in case we needed anything.

description: Holidaycottages.co.uk - Personally inspected Holiday Cottages for you across England, Wales and Scotland. Voted 'Gold' for customer service by Feefo.
title: Lovely cottage with absolutely…
review: Lovely cottage with absolutely everything you need. Comfy furniture, comfy bed and great pillows!  Well laid out and tastefully decorated. Highlight was the hot tub which we used every evening after long walks on various beaches. Ideally situated for exploring north and south.

description: Holidaycottages.co.uk - Personally inspected Holiday Cottages for you across England, Wales and Scotland. Voted 'Gold' for customer service by Feefo.
title: Wonderful stay at The Retreat
review: We had a wonderful stay in The Retreat. Beautiful location, Very clean and comfortable. Hot tub was an added bonus. Bournemouth and Sandbanks 15/20 drive away, Christchurch 10 mins away. Lovely pubs close by. Hamper was a lovely surprise, homemade Victoria sponge, fresh bread and milk and Prosecco. I’ll 💯  be go back

description: Holidaycottages.co.uk - Personally inspected Holiday Cottages for you across England, Wales and Scotland. Voted 'Gold' for customer service by Feefo.
title: Beautiful, cosy & tranquil Pods
review: Just enjoyed a fabulous 4 night stay, pod was perfect - so cosy, stunning views & the Hot Tub was most welcoming after long walks, we were lucky to have a dusting of snow - which made the whole cosiness setting so much more tranquil, couldn’t fault a thing!!!Thank you Elain & John for being perfect hosts.Melanie & Martin xx

description: Holidaycottages.co.uk - Personally inspected Holiday Cottages for you across England, Wales and Scotland. Voted 'Gold' for customer service by Feefo.

review: Pretty cottage in a beautiful location with easy access to Harrogate.Well equipped. Everything in working order and very clean.So warm and comfortable with lovely views overlooking fields of sheep. Thoughtful personal touches from the owners.We stayed for a week over Christmas. Owners had provided  a Christmas tree and mince pies for our arrival. We would highly recommend and hope to make future visits.

description: Holidaycottages.co.uk - Personally inspected Holiday Cottages for you across England, Wales and Scotland. Voted 'Gold' for customer service by Feefo.
title: Fabulous cottage
review: Beautiful cottage! Perfect for a family celebration.Location great for exploring the beaches of west wales. Cosy and warm with the fire and underfloor heating making it perfect for winter stays. Hot tub great for relaxing just give time for it to warm up with it being wood fired.

description: Holidaycottages.co.uk - Personally inspected Holiday Cottages for you across England, Wales and Scotland. Voted 'Gold' for customer service by Feefo.

review: The perfect property and location for our 10 guests.  Amazing views, 18 minute easy walk to a great pub.  Loads of walking options - we decided to focus on Crummock Water and Loweswater so we didn’t need to drive.  A wonderful weeks holiday

description: Holidaycottages.co.uk - Personally inspected Holiday Cottages for you across England, Wales and Scotland. Voted 'Gold' for customer service by Feefo.
title: Really lovely stay
review: Really lovely stay. Especially loved the luxurious soft towels and robes .Also the warm hot tub. The welcome hamper full of local produce was great. As was a pint of milk for an immediate cuppa. Would definitely recommend.

description: Holidaycottages.co.uk - Personally inspected Holiday Cottages for you across England, Wales and Scotland. Voted 'Gold' for customer service by Feefo.

review: Our stay was made even more special with the thoughtful touches from Beth and James such as the lovely welcome board and basket in the hallway, to the Xmas pies, mulled wine, and bottle of bubbly on the kitchen island. The very informative Web page was professionally done with everything you needed to know for your stay.

description: Holidaycottages.co.uk - Personally inspected Holiday Cottages for you across England, Wales and Scotland. Voted 'Gold' for customer service by Feefo.

review: Great cosy cottage, welcoming host and everything as described. Photos didn’t do the property justice as it was alot bigger than expected. Would definitely go with this company again. Very good location for seeing the Yorkshire dales and moors. We had a fabulous time.

description: Holidaycottages.co.uk - Personally inspected Holiday Cottages for you across England, Wales and Scotland. Voted 'Gold' for customer service by Feefo.

review: Clean and lovely property with a hot tub and pool table. Very comfy sofas and a large family table for dinners meant out group of 10 was always comfortable and able to spend time together as a big group. Sophie was lovely and met us onsite to give keys and she had left all the ingredients For a lovely cream tea.

description: Holidaycottages.co.uk - Personally inspected Holiday Cottages for you across England, Wales and Scotland. Voted 'Gold' for customer service by Feefo.
title: Great
review: Great apartment, complete with everything we needed for our stay. Comfortable, clean rooms, plenty of space and practical for a walking holiday. Loved the grounds and walks straight from the door and an easy route into Hawkshead. Great base for exploring the lakes. We would definitely stay again.

description: Holidaycottages.co.uk - Personally inspected Holiday Cottages for you across England, Wales and Scotland. Voted 'Gold' for customer service by Feefo.
title: Superb location and views  …
review: Superb location within short walking  distance of local shops , pubs and restaurants (ps also lovely pub next door) Excellent views of the river which is right outside Cosy cottage with log burner and everything you need for a weekend get away

description: Holidaycottages.co.uk - Personally inspected Holiday Cottages for you across England, Wales and Scotland. Voted 'Gold' for customer service by Feefo.
title: Helen and Richard’s hospitality was…
review: Helen and Richard’s hospitality was warm and welcoming and Helen was brilliant at guiding us in on a foggy dark evening and welcomed us with Christmas tree lights and a warm cosy hut. The hut itself is a jem, cosy and inviting with all you could need for a seriously relaxing get away. The views are incredible, the sheep across the fence gorgeous and curious and the hot tub was bliss! We cannot wait to book again. Thank you both!

description: Holidaycottages.co.uk - Personally inspected Holiday Cottages for you across England, Wales and Scotland. Voted 'Gold' for customer service by Feefo.

review: Great support from customer service.    Wanted somewhere quiet for NYE (firework free zone) they were great in finding out if there were any likely displays in the vicinity.

description: Holidaycottages.co.uk - Personally inspected Holiday Cottages for you across England, Wales and Scotland. Voted 'Gold' for customer service by Feefo.
title: Very comfortable and cosy cottage
review: Very comfortable and cosy cottage. The views were amazing and the location perfect. We could walk to local pubs and eateries within minutes, or jump on the train to explore the wider area.The cottage was very well equipped and perfect for absolute relaxation.

description: Holidaycottages.co.uk - Personally inspected Holiday Cottages for you across England, Wales and Scotland. Voted 'Gold' for customer service by Feefo.
title: Great location - would recommend
review: Great location, perfect host. Very clean. Hot tub was fantastic. Loved the reclining seats on the sofa & the chair. Lovely warm house. Perfect retreat. Would highly recommend.

description: Holidaycottages.co.uk - Personally inspected Holiday Cottages for you across England, Wales and Scotland. Voted 'Gold' for customer service by Feefo.
title: The accomodation was top class
review: The accomodation was top class. And Tywyn is a fabulous location. for a Christmas break. Sadly we had a few human errors issues with our travelling dates. Asking for an extra 75 pounds sterling to make an enquiry to the owners of the property in our minds is a steep request. We unfortunately will not be using Holiday Cottages again due to that fact. Other websites are so much user friendly for accomodating a booking that needs to be amended. We have been regular visitors to  Wales over the years. We would stay in Pebbles in a heartbeat again if they would have us.. It's a fabulous property in a friendly location.

description: Holidaycottages.co.uk - Personally inspected Holiday Cottages for you across England, Wales and Scotland. Voted 'Gold' for customer service by Feefo.
title: A Bonny Tottie Hut
review: It is hard to be critical, as we had a lovely stay, but storage was limited for 2 people, a shelf in the bathroom and a couple of additional pillows would have made it perfect. In addition, the external decorative lights made the hut look amazing, but they continually tapped against the hut walls throughout the night. It would have been great if we could have had the option to unhook them during the windy nights.

description: Holidaycottages.co.uk - Personally inspected Holiday Cottages for you across England, Wales and Scotland. Voted 'Gold' for customer service by Feefo.
title: Hassle free seaside break
review: Hassle free break, easy to find on website and truthful description. Payment easy in 2 parts and helpful email reminders keep you on track with what you need to know. Always use Holiday Cottages for our breaks.

description: Holidaycottages.co.uk - Personally inspected Holiday Cottages for you across England, Wales and Scotland. Voted 'Gold' for customer service by Feefo.
title: Three generations for christmas
review: The location and layout were perfect for a family Christmas meet up.  The owner was super-helpful, answering questions ahead of time (e.g. is the oven big enough for a 6kg turkey).  Great quality bedding and linens, but the house would benefit from a deep clean. Some thoughtful additions for older guests e.g. non-slip shower mats, step-edges marked, place to sit while removing shoes.

description: Holidaycottages.co.uk - Personally inspected Holiday Cottages for you across England, Wales and Scotland. Voted 'Gold' for customer service by Feefo.
title: Charles the host was very pleasant
review: Charles the host was very pleasant. The property is well equipped and was clean.The log burner was a nice touch. Location is perfect for walkers, direct access to the canal that leads to Talybont.The pubs were never open in the village, but there is a delightful cafe and village shop. Don’t do to the Usk hotel/ b&b very rude. Google describes it as a hotel its not it is just rooms and the owner was not very forgiving when we turned up seeing if they served food and drink. Rather than saying no sorry, he was very abrupt through his roof top camera and forgot to deactivate when he used bad language at us with a 8 year old present. We digress and is nothing to do with this property. The location is perfect, close to Brecon and other towns. Good bus links to them from the A40. As already advised to our host, the only disappointment is the property is described as having a hot tub. They are not hot tubs, they are lazy spas which lacked maintenance. For that reason it did not get 5 stars. Everything else was perfect.Communication with the host was excellent. We are hoping to return in February and April.

description: Holidaycottages.co.uk - Personally inspected Holiday Cottages for you across England, Wales and Scotland. Voted 'Gold' for customer service by Feefo.
title: Perfect for Family Christmas
review: This property is lovely and the location is perfect. We were a family of 10 and the house provides ample space for all to relax. The PlayStation is a good addition and having a tumble dryer to dry children's onesies etc was a bonus. This is the second time we have stayed at the house over Christmas and the Christmas decorations makes it so much more perfect.We enjoyed the Polar Express at Swanage railway and Nutley Farm having a light display was beautiful. We also recommend the local pub, the Red Lion.
