Had to order a second jacket in a different size, and then return the original order once I knew the other size was right. This was a little fiddly given returns aren’t free and there’s a 14 day limitation, but it worked out fine and I had my refund through quickly for the returned item.

I’d have bought the rim tape if it had said it wasn’t already fitted, the absence of such a basic requirement on the part of the wheel manufacturer seeming a bit odd.

title: Win win situation
review: I bought some MTB Tyres after having had a disappointing experience with a different seller. The tyres were sold as "soiled" although I didn't notice this until after I had paid for them. However, when they arrived the soiling was minimal and the huge reduction in price was very welcome. Really pleased that I didn't cancel the order. Someone made a very good ethical decision to sell these perfectly good but slightly dirty tyres at a very good price. A win all round.

description: We're dedicated to providing you with the very best of sport and leisure goods, with an emphasis on quality, competitive pricing and great customer services.

They also docked me 10% for damage to the package which is reasonable as the post office made a hash of wrapping it. My only complaint is that it took nearly 4 weeks to get the refund. Other than that the product I didn't return (chalk bag) is good.

Lately, I have found the Schwalbe road tyres come up bigger for a given size than say, Continental.

title: Sport and Leisure 👍
review: Peruzzo Zephyr 2                         Tow Bar Mounted Bike CarrierThis was a well priced quality carrier, excellent delivery service. The bike rack was  fully assembled on taking it out of the box.On inspection it was evident that the two short cross members were misaligned, upright handle grips missing and the tyre holders were the wrong way around.Sport and Leisure were proactive in swiftly resolving all of the above issues,Peruzzo were not so forthcoming.It appears that this rack was poorly assembled by the manufacturers who offered no plausible answers to my concerns .It's annoying that these minor niggles weren't addressed at source as they distracted from a well specced piece of kit, competitively priced especially with e bay offering a 20% discount code .The rack is not too heavy, it holds my two e bikes safely and securely,the ramp makes loading easy and the lockable components are reassuring . Overall very pleased .

After much pushing with tweezers it’s pretty much back in position and switching on and off ok but I’ll need to handle it with care.

Got my money back but my bike is still off the road and I'll have to find some time to go to my local bike shop and get some tyres.

review: I would have liked my new SRAM cassette to arrive in its original packaging as I don't know if I have a genuine part

review: Prompt delivery 👍But Rim was not as good a quality as the first one I bought of same model Join in rim there was a gap, un like previous one also decals were full of bubbles and coming off won't stick as there was some kind of oil on the rim Bit disappointed really but what can you expect for £20 ?

description: We're dedicated to providing you with the very best of sport and leisure goods, with an emphasis on quality, competitive pricing and great customer services.
title: Zefal 1Litre Bottles
review: Zefal 1Litre Bottles - I ordered 2 of these bottles for cycling.  First thing I noticed was that the design isn't great.   Whilst the large opening allows for easy filling with energy powders/ice etc, the mouthpiece is very short and has to be bitten to allow the liquid out.  The design doesn't make this easy.  Secondly, on my first ride, one bottle jumped out of my bottle cage.  Not the fault of the bottle, but when it landed it cracked on impact and had to be thrown away.  I would have expected them to take much more abuse.  Wouldn't buy again.

description: We're dedicated to providing you with the very best of sport and leisure goods, with an emphasis on quality, competitive pricing and great customer services.

review: Not fitted it yet, but great looking chainset at a great price!Delivered quickly too.Only downside is that the product description could have/should have been more clearly written - I read it and thought that a bottom bracket was included. 'Fraid not!

I should have been more vigilant regarding the left/right/both options but it would be best if they forced you to select an option.    Regarding the brake wire, when I queried the company they said they are only supplied when the whole set is purchased, pointedly saying this was specified in the description.   For that reason I returned the Left changer purchased ( I had to pay for the postage!) and ordered the whole set only to receive the full set without any brake cables!!

description: We're dedicated to providing you with the very best of sport and leisure goods, with an emphasis on quality, competitive pricing and great customer services.

I've had an "expert" apparently looking at the pics I sent them of a faulty item for over 2 weeks now and no reply email from them after I've chased a resolution repeatedly...  just get, almost daily, "feedback/survey" spam emails which is very annoying when they haven't got back to me about a refund or replacement for faulty product.  I've spent a lot of money here too so it's very disappointing

What on earth is OE? This is mentioned at the very end of the product description, but to the average consumer, OE means nothing.

Unfortunately I would not recommend using this company.

review: ... or is it going to be month or year? - that the BBC finally decides not to show needles going into arms with such dull, graphic frequency.We get the point. *I will also celebrate the day when its reasonably paid, high quality journalists discipline themselves to, by single example, speak proper. To both say and write 'has' where grammatically correct as opposed to almost universally instead using 'have' would be a great start. **Some does. Most doesn't. Innit. Whatever happened to BBC English? By example:The BBC  HAS decided not to show needles going into arms all the damned time  The next of kin HAS been informed Liverpool HAS not had a good run of form lately The European Union HAS not yet decided either way. Oh, but it will at the very last minute. It's simple, shurely. For singular, use 'has.'For plural... yep, you has got the idea. Odd exceptions excepted. Pull your socks up, BBC. Please. .. Even Jim can't fix this, it seems.On the plus side.. ? Despite quite a relentless bashing since our Jim did indeed fix it and, out of respect to him, we all then got to know about it in 2011, I consider BBC News to be the most trustworthy media outlet globally. Even though it is indisputably left leaning. Just look at the Newsnight staff. For e.g. Emily Maitlis, Kirsty Walk, Lewis Goodhall... really rather LEFT. But, entertaining nonetheless. Its a programme I enjoy very much. BBC's newsreaders are well worth separate attention; top dogs, me thinks: each and every. And, thank Gawd (or whoever we may currently be allowed to refer to), all lack the sometime-melodrama of ITN and so, inherently resist adding their pennyworth to serious news items. Tom Bradby would not do well at the BBC because he would not be encouraged to crocodile-tear his conclusion to a sad story. Or frown at the baddies. And that would make him very sad. On the lighter stories, the BBC also get it just right. Sorry, gets it just right. Oh, it doesn't matter. Martin Croxall and Simone McCoy handle those little babies with especial aplomb. Oh, that twinkle. And Front Cover Tom, the naughty weather doll, has his moments also.But.. (And?).. .. It's true, it's true.. 1. I do believe it subliminally represents itself rather too well and too often as left-biased (BBC in general, across its political output) 2. I do believe it very shoddily and grudgingly represented any pro Brexit standpoint 3. I do believe that, post-Savile, Management has - or is it 'have?'-crawled up its own b/side many times with what has seemed a squalid frenzied attempt at latent 'political correctness.'And such a stupid phrase, that. There, I've said it. Much like 'Multiculturism.' Phrases manufactured and designed to shut you up. There, I've said it. Again. The MOOBOSO club (mock-outrage-on-behalf-of-silent-others) will be out for my blood now. Toughen up, Beeb. You are NOT now always the demon. Defend your position, occasionally. But... the BBC is still, as I see it - and, at this rate per word, this is all that matters now - streets ahead of any other news outlet. The World knows it too. Except China, enraged innocents that they are. Sorry, it is. Credit where it's due ? Call it tough love. And I do love them. I do. Sorry, it. xx*****P.S. I feel I must note that, as I write, the 97% 'bad' rating across all reviewers of BBC News is, just patently ridiculous. And this, while the other 5% (somewhat confusingly) grace BBC News with something at least more enthusiastic than that. The 97% 'bad' figure otherwise speaks volumes that those who choose to review on sites such as these, do so disproportionately out of an 'outraged, self-nurtured' anger.Perhaps, then, less so out of a desire for wild praise. Trustpilot and others ferment the 'all or nothing' reviewer, I suppose. That's a lamentable reflection on all of us here. Across the board, that is to say. As for me.. excuse me while I adjust my halo. Speak for yourself !* Much improved since original posting. (We thank you) ** Still waiting. Innit.

title: BBC is great!! Not so for BBC News…

Radio 4 and and Radio 6 programmes are exceptionally good!  TBH, my life would be much more empty without it.My issue is with the political news and the reporters. For some reason it seems that the Beeb often allow outright lies and falsehoods to go completely unchallenged. This seems to be a general rule for most government ministers, but I also see it when reporters question opposition party's and other political commentators. Additionally, reporters often fail to ask blatantly obvious questions of political interviewees. To me it appears that the guest have dictated the terms of the interview before they agree to be interviewed. If this is the case, it should never be allowed in a functioning democracy, when talking to MP's. All MP's work for the people of these islands, all those that choose to appear on BBC news programmes must be ready to justify their statements to the people. The BBC should be the voice of the people (after all we pay for it) and it should not allow politicians, or think tank representatives or anybody else to go unchallenged on what they say. If not, then don't invite them to comment and report on the news subject anyway. Also, please stop reading out written statements as a response to a given subject. These are often used by indivduals or groups that are afriad to be challaged. If the characters concerned in a story are not available or unwillingly to appear then tough, run the story anyway.  I understand that there is a policy of impartially in place, but it is evident to all, that the policy is getting in the way of what used to be great journalism, or it is simply being used as an excuse for failure to properly address the concerns of the viewing public. Poor political journalism, leads to poor politicians. To those at the BBC if you read this, please bring back the great days of Paxman, Day and Frost and please grow a pair for the good of the country. That said, I still love the BBC, just not BBC News.

review: OK if you live in London - we live in Surrey but I'm from Doncaster originally, forget any national news focus on the North, we only merit a quick vox-pop from some northern shopping centres.  For example the nationwide loss of manufacturing and poor national investment/ transport links never makes it into the national BBC news - all seems to be about tube trains and London bubble news.Awash with the ArtsThe move to Manchester appears to be for light programs and production, BBC feels like it's essentially a London broadcasting corporation:BBC should either represent the UK - or - the government ought to remove their licence fee and allow it to be a state news organ/ state information broadcaster.BBC Radio shows invariably voice their characters as Northern if they are either agitators or uneducated. The working class of the South it seems are equally unrepresented in any Radio format except the Archers.Place an urbane BBC 'hero' character with erudition against an unruly mob and the mob characters all begin speaking with northern accents - perhaps a reflection of the BBCs decision to recruit heavily from Oxbridge - or a lack of decentralisation; title: A strange Christmas music programme
review: Few radio programmes have made me more angry than “Radio 3 in Concert: A concert of Christmas music” broadcast on 18 December 2024.  (1) I tuned in, expecting to listen to the glories of Christmas music from over the centuries, with perhaps musical offerings from Poland, Belgium, Germany, Italy, the UK, North America, to name but a few.  And there was indeed a promising start with Gaudete! However, the music soon deteriorated in quality: it was more like listening to a Christmas edition of “Uncle Tom’s Cabin”, with what sounded like coolies chanting.  No doubt places like Nigeria, Eritrea, Somalia, etc have their own composers and musical traditions.  But how relevant are those obscure musical traditions to main-stream European music and culture today?  Practically zero, I would suggest, though perhaps fascinating to someone researching musical traditions, language development for a higher degree, or someone whose head is crammed full of Woke rubbish.  It was rather like turning on BBC Radio 4 for the news, only to find that the news is read in the Sichuan dialect of Mandarin: culturally discordant, meaningless.  I switched off my radio in disgust, turning it on again a few minutes later in the hope that the music had improved.  It hadn’t, so I didn’t bother with the rest of this programme.  Did someone actually get paid for compiling this crap on Radio 3 on 18 December?  Did the presenter need a few whiskies before commencing this cringe-worthy Woke anthology of Christmas music?(2) In the Third Reich, in modern China, Iran, Russia, North Korea, and several other places today, the slavish acceptance of dogma is the unquestioned norm.  Similarly, at the BBC today, one finds analogies to brain-washing and dogma in the form of critical race theory, and diversity, equality and inclusivity claptrap.  At the BBC, the total absence of well-founded critical thinking now seems to permeate all its levels.   Does 2+3=green?  Is a straight line really a sphere?  Is black really white?  Maybe “up” actually means “down”?  Some people are not even sure what “a woman” is, including our present Prime Minister!  Universities today are no longer places where students learn HOW to think: universities have become indoctrination factories where you are told WHAT to think!  Society seems to be developing more cretinous tendencies with each passing year: the relentless weakening of mental processes.(3) The BBC seems to have swallowed Woke mind-numbing drivel hook, line and sinker.  And of course this is the same organisation that paid £1.3 million a year to a former Walker’s crisps salesman for his commentaries on “Match of the Day”.  And it is also the BBC that formerly employed dodgy characters like Jimmy Saville, Frank Bough, Stuart Hall, and Greg Wallace to add to its steadily increasing roll of shame.  How many more skeletons-in-the-cupboard are still waiting to be discovered before this bullshit dogma is finally exposed and rooted out: a dangerous virus that has taken hold of the brains in the not-so-brainy?The BBC’s comeuppance is long overdue.  It richly deserves being cut down to size from its preposterous stances!

title: Misleading
review: Received an email within minutes of starting the 'subscription' saying 4 to 6 weeks for the first magazine, quite a shock as I had put the subscription to start with the August edition. The only option to pay was by Direct Debit, two weeks later they have not applied a Direct Debit to the account, it seems that I can forget the August edition. I called the customer service number on the isubscribe website to check if all was well, the lady involved worked at the actual magazine I had subscribed to, they have no record of the subscription, the customer number given by iSubscribe was not in their format. I also mentioned that the website said that the magazine's publishers would be applying the Direct Debit and be paid directly, they said this would not happen, it was against their privacy policy to take banking details from a third party. There is no number to call isubcribe directly, the only number they give is for the magazine publishers who quite frankly have no idea what is going on. So it appears I have given my bank details, all my personal details and believe I had set up a subscription for a magazine to receive nothing but misinformation. I contacted them by their contact form, received an automated reply saying it would be 4 to 6 weeks, an industry standard before I would receive my subscription. Strange, I have subscribed with other magazines in the past, received a magazine with in the week and been allowed to pay via credit card. I have asked for this 'subscription' to be cancelled. I await their reply and will amend the review as required. Reply received a week later, blames the publisher who still does not know who I am or anything about a subscription. iSubcribe tells me to email the publisher to cancel business with iSubscribe even though it has been cancelled in writing to them 7 days. I would advise anyone to subscribe directly with a magazine ad in iSubscribe's mindset that is what you are doing as they seem to wash their hands of you as soon as you hit the buy button and just pass all your detail or not, to a third party. Two weeks have passed and a direct debit for DC Thomson has appeared on my account even through DC Thomson has said in writing there is no subscription and iSubscribe are fully aware that the subscription is a subscription that was cancelled weeks ago and have not reply to my emails. I begin to wonder if iSubscribe is run from someone's kitchen table. The direct debit has been cancelled, I'm gobsmacked that DC Thompson have used my banking details when it is against their own privacy policy. I have just received an email from DC Thompson that says they did receive instruction from iSubscribe within the last week and have cancelled the subscription as soon as it was received, they apparently do not have my banking details, yet that does no explain why DC Thompson have set up a direct debit.

Not what I wanted.- They have a 48 hour no commitment cancellation period, so I cancel immediately via e-mail. Blocked!- Worst of all, when you do get the info from the actual publisher, there is no 12 month minimum contract!! This was just something outdated on the rather clunky isubscribe website. There was no need to cancel!I wish I could have just gone direct to the publisher (David Hall) who actually have a customer service helpline as they seemed much more responsive!

title: Good reliable and quick service, just ensure you check the lenses are clean before using.
review: I hired two lenses,  the canon 24-70 f/2.8 and 70-200 f.2.8 IS. They were great and enabled me to create some superb images. In terms of the ordering and delivery systems they were delivered and returned without issue and all reserved online without any problems. Although the lenses were great (a thank you more to canon) and the delivery / ordering system of lenses for hire were straight forward I was not overly impressed by the condition the lenses were delivered in. I am a professional photographer and keep all of my equipment including lenses immaculately clean. This ensures longevity and also that you don't a) get undesired marks in your photos from the optics being dirty and b) get dust on your sensor from unclean lens base optics. I ordered two lenses but the two separate packages only contained one return label between them. Not a big issue but I was surprised as lenses for hire supply all of the packaging to return the lens safely which is great. I was just a little concerned that a lens could get lost. The labels have codes for each lens on them so I replicated the missing label using the correct code found on the packing sheet for that specific lens. Secondly both lenses required the optics cleaning. They both had dust on the outside of filter and the inside of the filter. The 24-70 lens was clean on the actual optic however the 70-200mm lens required the optic to be cleaned also. On the 70-200mm the base optic velvet material was dusty and had what looked like tissue residue on it. Lastly the lens caps on both lenses were dirty and the 70-200mm had what looked like mud encrusted in the rim. I ended up using 4 lens wipes and 30 minutes of my time. I of course always invest time in to cleaning my lenses after the are used however I did not expect to have to clean the hired lenses at my own cost before I used them.

The day of the project. As I was scheduled to leave the house at 4 am, that meant that I had to cancel the project. So I had to leave without the lens that was delivered to my adress at 10h50, that´s 50 minutes behind schedule! I contacted LensForHire to explain the facts, strangely I never got a reply with an explanation or an apology; I only got the auto-reply emails explaining what to do to return the lens! After my return from France I booked the lens return courier. This time LensForHire choose JCA Courier. I called them to book the return and unbelievably they told me that the company that was doing the pick-up was City Links, subcontracted by JCA. I asked JCA when the pick-up was to take place and how could I contact City Links; their reply was that City Links could not be contacted and did not work with period slot bookings, they only guarantied pick-up between 9hH30 and 17H30 on 16th June. The lens was finally picked up at 15H30; I had to wait at home for almost a full working day to see my LensForHire saga come to an end.

title: Product - Fautless // Customer Service = non-existent
review: It's a shame. I had a brilliant experience 1st time round. However, tried the same company again and we've hit a brick wall. I've taken an e-mail I sent nearly 2 weeks ago that i've yet to have a reply to: {quote} Dear Lens for hire, Just had a chat with a member of your team on the phone. Must say I'm rather disappointed. Let me first put my hands up and explain to you in writing that I've made a mistake with my order. It's only by noticing the dispatched email just sent that I noticed I've ordered for the wrong weekend. I in fact require the lens next weekend not this weekend. As was repeatedly mentioned on the phone, I'd read and replied to previous emails with the current booked date range. An oversight by me as I'd simply been looking at the wrong weekend on the calendar. Now, I understand you are a money making business with overheads etc but I've come back to you as a repeat customer in trust. Especially as you are not the cheapest in the market. That trust has been knocked after this experience as I'm politely told on the phone my only option is to pay an additional £47 to extend my booking for the additional days into the weekend I want (I'm not preventing anybody else from using the lens according the website) or return it and lose my money entirely.  I'm a little backed into a corner here. How's that good customer service?  I appreciate it's my mistake but a business that forces somebody to either lose their money or pay extra isn't going to win any new business. It's completely inflexible!  The product is good but on this occasion your customer service is not. No flexibility or understanding whatsoever. I'm unlikely to be recommending your company to my colleagues in the photographic world going forward.    {unquote}  I've yet to receive a response to my question and notice my bank statement shows an additional charge.  POOR POOR POOR!!!

Phone call to be told my application would ‘likely’ be rejected due to a late payment, £100 application fee, but my luck it got accepted, give you 5 months to look for a house? Found my dream house, sale agreed,  found issues in the inspection,  give them a 3 week to fix it, rejected. So we’re already 10 weeks away from the deadline, so how am I meant to find another property in the next 10 weeks before meeting the deadline???? The issue in the house could’ve been resolved as I had planned for someone to look at it, but Co ownership does not allow this, £550 property assessment and £440 returned (which took a week to get refunded), who can actually be bothered with this type of stress?? Does this ‘charity’ think people have all the money in the world to waste on property assessments when trying to buy a house?? This is meant to be something to help people to get into the property ladder, but make it impossible to do so. So save your money kids and go for a mortgage, also a lot of vendors purposely avoid Co ownership applications because of the length of time ‘waste of time’ it takes to do applications. Btw, 1.8 million people in Northern Ireland and this only owns 10,000, meaning it’s not even 1% of them in NI. Do not be fooled . Edit: from the response, so in 10 weeks I’m meant to find a house, get sale agreed (most vendors avoid Co own) pay another £550 for an assessment, and then have to wait another 3 weeks for it to fall through? Is ir meant to be ping pong until the deadline to the point I don’t have a house in the end? Instead I’m wasting £200+ ? This is not worth the stress and the horror stories are to be believed.

Altogether this process took 7months.I found a house I absolutely fell in love with and thought I could live there. Well... After paying the valuator to come out, he stated it wasn't worth the offer I put in and Co-ownership stated I wouldn't be getting that house.Then I had to find another property which was another joke. The other property I found I had to pay another valuator to come out obviously which stated I had to fix a retaining wall (which was 4 foot out of my property and holding up 6 other houses) that was averaging around £5000.  I was told by a company that the wall Co-ownership discussed about was part of the council and to dig up the retaining wall, it would involve destruction of gardens in the surrounding area.  Later I had to withdraw my offer on that property as Co-ownership were taking too much time and at this stage I had 3 weeks left before I had to move out.I then thought I would get in contact with the estate agent that I originally had an offer with about a house I absolutely loved.  I had to pay a valuator (AGAIN ON THE SAME PROPERTY) to state it was worth lower and didnt have as much problems as the first one stated.So I finally got into the house I originally wanted at the very start. The stress I went through was an absolute joke and wouldn't wish it on anyone. I advise everyone to just save and get a mortgage, don't bother with Co-ownership as it was a disgrace.

title: BUYER BEWARE
review: In February 2019 my wife and I, having reached our late 60's decided to put our funeral arrangements in order. We chose Fosters as the plan they offered was comprehensive and a good price. Their agent came to our home and after a short time we decided to initiate a Fosters Funeral Plan for each of us. A week or so later our plans arrived in the post, and  after checking the salient details consigned  the plans to our documents folio. Fast forward to the present day , having paid Fosters since the start of our plans we were wondering when our packages would be paid up and took the plans out to check them. We were puzzled that the figures we were paying on the plan did not jibe with a total amount for either 60 or 72 months of payments for our requested plan. We read our contracts (which we should have done at the start of our association with Fosters but didn't) to find the following details in the small print. We did not sign up for an easy pay plan for the cost of our packages, rather we had signed up for an All of Life insurance plan which will mature upon our deaths or when we reach the age of 90.It was our error to believe that Fosters would not seek to mislead us in any way. However at our friendly meeting with their agent the term "All of Life Policy " was never mentioned. Had it been mentioned we would never have signed up for a 20 year payment plan. In closing we hope that anyone who takes out such a plan with any funeral director takes the time to read all of the documents sent to them by their chosen company. Please do not trust that these people are acting in your best interests as they are not and not all of your financial commitments will be explained to you.

title: My family used this company for my cousins funeral AVOID
review: My family used this company for my cousins funeral and what can I say other than than it was the  worst experience ever from beginning to end.Day 1 they messed up picking the body up and the whole funeral was held back nearly a week , after that there was mistake after mistake the person who was appointed to arrange the funeral  was hopeless never kept us updated on anything never called when they said they would and every time  we had to call back it was different people that we spoke to who did not know what was happening , absolutely no communication from anyone the service was diabolical, now given this company is dealing with grieving families they have a lot to learn When it comes to showing empathy and putting the grieving families feelings  to the front and foremost at all times , all they done was make the loss of her son even harder for my auntie to bare.After everything that they messed up the day of the funeral came  and the hearse showed up without the spray of flowers on the coffin my auntie was distraught no apology was offered just business as usual for theses guys,  they are a disgrace and during the full process not once did I see a caring side to any of them.So the final kick in the teeth came after the funeral when my auntie went to collect her sons ashes and pay the bill , however they had made a blunder and sent the bill to the wrong address so they then proceeded to tell her that she wasn’t the client infact it was her ex husband and she would need his permission to get her sons ashes , the level of disgust that I felt for fosters funeral services at that point was really starting to show , this was yet again another mistake made by them and rather than show empathy and admit there mistake the fosters  had the absolute cheek to tell my auntie who by this point was inconsolable that it was data protection and she must have allowed this , all I can say is wow where is your compassion where is your duty of care ?I proceeded to put in a formal complaint through head office while outside I was  assured  that I would be called back the next day by a complaints manager that was over a week ago and guess what I am still waiting .This company is a disgrace and I would not recommend to anyone to use infact  my advice would be to AVOID at all costs these people failed my auntie in more ways than one they are the worst company I have ever came across  , you only get one chance at giving your loved ones the best send off they deserve and when you choose a funeral director who you put  all of your trust in to carry everything out with the finest Attention to detail and then you are let down by poor judgment and mistake after mistake with no empathy or care shown this cannot be changed so please think carefully before even considering using this company.

description:
We are Homemade Homes the experienced property sales team within Accent Housing. Homemade Homes by Accent is a brand name for the sale of homes owned by Accent Housing Limited and Accent Homemade Limited.
We specialise in Shared Ownership, another way to buy your home. You buy a percentage and pay rent on the rest. We own just part of it – but you’re living there, you decorate it and decide when to sell.
Buying a percentage means a smaller deposit and a smaller mortgage. It’s a sooner first step on the ladder for lots of people. Usually, you can carry on buying further shares to own it 100%.
Buying a share means you need a lower mortgage and deposit than purchasing a property outright. This makes it a cost-effective way to own your own home and ideal for first-time buyers. Shared Ownership usually works out less per month than renting privately.
We want to be ‘with you for your journey’, whether that is helping you to take the first step onto the housing ladder or helping you search for a new home, we will be right there with you.
We have Shared Ownership homes across the country, from Surrey to Yorkshire and have helped hundreds of people fulfil their home ownership ambitions. We offer new and resale Shared Ownership homes as well as helping our current customers buy more of their home or sell it when they want to move on.

title: Aftercare? Ongoing problems.
review: When I paid the reservation fee, I discovered that the garden gate was completely dislodged and broken. They told me it had been repaired before I bought the house. However, the repair work was done hastily. The gate is not fixed in place and the lock does not fit into the lock hole. Despite reporting this multiple times, it still hasn’t been replaced with a new one or properly secured. Additionally, when the driveway was constructed, it was sloped towards the front of my house instead of the drainage, causing all the rainwater to accumulate in front of my house. Also, the fences started coming loose in just six months, and I see rusty nails every day. I noticed that the houses in the same development that are not shared ownership have better quality materials (doors, cupboards, etc.). The garden is not levelled, making it very difficult to place a table. When the boiler is running, it leaks water, which I reported, but no one has addressed it. Additionally, I mentioned the bulges on the wall, but again, no one has taken care of it.

review: Appalling customer service.Recommend independent complaints manager to replace cavalier one who doubles as manager I complained about!  Attempted purchase 11th March, and in spite of est agent being told in March electricity would be switched on and property cleaned, along with new 99 yr lease, this still hasn't happened 30th May!Recommend ALL legal docs collated as soon as property put on the market not MONTHS after sale agreed, and quit excuses like 'we didn't know whether the property would sell.'--cavalier attitude now impacting a whole series of decent honest people.Recommend Homemadehomes detail what's included in sale AND the location of it instead of expecting est agent to second guess where garage, additional storage, access is sited etc............Recommend checking all computerised docs so wrong ones sent to solicitor(six times!)cannot be idiotically blamed on the computer!Recommend that the lease is drawn up prior to advertising  NOT three/four/five/????? months after sale agreed. Sorry still waiting.................Recommend conveyancing begins as soon as sale agreed, as is normal, NOT ....sorry when are ALL legal docs to be sent to my sol?? Does this manager even know what conveyancing involves...her poor use of written language evidences she doesn't.Recommend manager put on an English course as her written comms is appalling---no experience of using technical terminology appropriately etc Answers any question except the one you ask, and gives gratutious information to cover up the fact she hasn't a clue about what she is talking about......e.g My Q.when will conveyancing begin?(asked over five times)Her Ans. I don't know when conveyancing will end!!!!!!!!My buyers are tearing their hair out, so am I at the total incompetence feeding the delay of a purchase which would in the real world take only eight weeks. The whole process is costing me money with a string of contractors wondering what is going on. In addition agencies that have dealt with this org fail to give positive appraisal unsurprisingly.Disgraceful company turning what should have been a simple swift cash purchase into a tour of insolence and poor management.'Resale purchase' used in reply demonstrates another abuse of terminology, why not just say 'purchase?' Also I would prefer using my solicitor for help with the purchase, who still awaits being sent all legal docs related to my purchase..........

Those are the things you'd only care when you start living in the place, of course... For example, doors and windows are quite heavy to pull ( they are well quality and secure, for sure); ensuite shower glass is too narrow to block the water from the shower splashing into the bathroom (which means extra mess and cleaning after use); bathtub in the 2nd bathroom is too high to get in or out; nice kitchen but deep / hard to reach cupboards below the counter, etc... In the overall, I thought Audley Coopers Hill could have done better if they paid attention to such practical details from a perspective of a resident that is not in need of a full-time carer and is fairly independent.

A great concept to encourage a sense of community participation by allowing the wider community to have use of the facilities this should help create a positive vibe. review: Our representative, Claire, was delightful—friendly, knowledgeable, and impeccably professional. Her assistance in addressing all our inquiries was invaluable.While the site is still primarily under construction, it’s easy to imagine the beauty of the village upon completion. The main complex is a beautiful listed building, although we had hoped the new houses would have been designed to harmonise with it. Nonetheless, the completed cottages are tastefully presented with charming potted plants adorning the petite front gardens and a cosy shared patio at the rear. Despite our expectation of seeing solar panels on the new buildings, we were informed that some would be placed atop the main building.The show house boasted exquisite decor and impeccable taste. The square rooms were generously sized, though storage space was notably limited. Underfloor heating is provided via heat pumps, and the well-appointed kitchen includes a washer-dryer. Interestingly, hanging out washing is discouraged, presumably to maintain the ambiance.The price tag, admittedly, was quite substantial. While one might naturally expect to pay for certain services within a gated community, the leasehold price for the house we viewed was substantially higher than we expected. Additionally, the monthly service charge was astonishing, with utilities and council tax excluded. Parking charges of £600 annually, limited to one car per residence, further added to the financial considerations. Personal assistance is available but comes at a cost. Ultimately, upon property sale, Audley retains nearly 30%.In conclusion, this holds the potential to be an exceptional place to reside, offering a wealth of amenities, activities, and social opportunities, provided that financial considerations are not a primary concern.

title: I first visited Coopers Hill
review: I first visited Coopers Hill, supposedly the flag ship, and found the staff almost rude. There is only one nice table in the coffee bar overlooking the garden and it was occupied by the staff. This is surely not right? This experience put me off.However a couple of years later I thought I would book an overnight stay to give it one more chance. I spoke to some one who was polite, explained my desire to stay overnight to see if it was for me. She was pleasant and welcoming. She put me through to Hannah who apparently could book me in. Rarely have I experienced such RUDENESS, amongst other things she told me it was not a hotel in a very unpleasant tone. As if I didn’t know that. I asked to speak to a manager and was told it’s not possible and an unknown manger would call me back tomorrow and there is not complaints number. Surely you can handle complaints better than that? Might help you to avoid bad reviews and encourage you to sort out your staff. Manners cost noting and count for a lot. UPDATE. Two days later.  I have still not receive the promised call back from a different manager. So I called back myself. Spoke to Alan this time: who was flustered wanted me to tell him all the gory details. I asked him : “surely the details should be discussed with a manager as management lol you need to know is it is a complaint about a manager ?” He still kept asking, even after I told him he could not find a manager, could not give me a number, said someone would call me back, and of course they did not!!Is this really how a supposed 5 star service deals with complaints. They must have an awful lot of them as they are so busy. Beware, I dread to think how residents might be treated considering how a prospective client has been treated

Further, Staci claimed she had previously emailed the solicitor, Erica John-Marie at Russell-Cooke to let them know the information about me filing bankruptcy was inaccurate. However, upon speaking with Erica, she stated that the matter remained unresolved. Interestingly, Fraser and Fraser’s website claims they pride themselves on commitment and clarity. My experience has proven this is far from the truth of how they actually run their practice. No commitnent, no follow up, no telephone call the next day and I have no idea if she is telling the truth about the email being sent to correct their mistake. And even the next day, she would not disclose how she came upon this false information and reported it in writing to someone else. Not even an apology. This exemplifies nothing short of a lack of candor, professionalism and communication.

Thanks a lot for making safeguarding accessible.

title: Not ideal for adult learners
review: I feel a lot more interest and enthusiasm would need to be generated by staff towards student's learning goals to make this a fulfilling experience for adults.  I didn't really feel my wish to learn was always met well.  If anything my enthusiasm was dampened by these classes.   To improve I think far more engagement, interest and indeed teaching needs to be given in line with what the adult wants to do.  It seemed as if it was up to me to get anywhere with this, I didn't feel met half way and I wasn't very much encouraged.Addressing the reply from ArtK I would like to make clear that I was invited to drop by on the phone when I rang to enquire about booking the classes.  It was not a free 1 to 1 private session by any means and not worth £27.50.  Moreover I have a flyer advertising free preliminary sessions for adults anyway, it says 'book your trial now' but that doesn't appear to be available on the website.  So the idea I got this private consultation free is misleading,  it was a chat, and there was another student there it wasn't one to one.  I did not know ArkK had CCTV cameras recording students and if I had known I wouldn't have gone, I wouldn't have been comfortable doing my art on camera.  Perhaps ArtK should be clear that they are recording people doing their art, some may not like it.Re the alleged free and 'bespoke' materials these were some pencils which I returned and a rubber.  Also I was given a drawing book but that's to be expected.  I asked for work to do at home but felt somewhat ridiculed for it at times.  I was told 'most people don't ask for homework' but I had paid and I wanted to learn and I wanted to practise at home.  I was given some ideas to work with at home when I asked but I wouldn't say I was much encouraged.This is not to say I learned nothing, I did learn but my initial review is truthful. When I spoke to customer service at ArtK about my experience they did not imply I was lying where here where I offer my honest review the respondent is almost saying 'CCTV footage shows you aren't truthful'.   I have to say I find the involvement of CCTV here quite concerning.   If I give Trustpilot a review I don't expect to be confronted with claims of evidence through me being recorded in a private learning setting in this very small studio.   I'm relating my experience and you are trawling footage to deny what I say about my experience.   ArtK should make it clear to customers that they are recording them throughout all the sessions.  There should be some indication in the studio that CCTV cameras are recording.  Thank you for your reply.  I won't be returning to ArtK especially given how my Trustpilot review has been handled as if it were a criminal case.

title: There should be a -100 star for this…
review: There should be a -100 star for this company and I’ll tell you what it is , I’ve always been someone who avoids debt. I’ve never liked credit cards( no matter how useful) or installment payments, and the thought of taking out a loan was completely against my value something I never in this life I thought I would ever do . However, this all changed when I joined Asset For Life’s serviced accommodation program.It started with a free Zoom call where they pitched their service accomodation program as a “done-for-you” service. I vividly remember being called  by CHARLIE that there were only five spots left. (You know how sales people can persuade😒and well they did put the pressure on me and won this one )When I mentioned I didn’t have the money, the pressure tactics began. They pushed me to take out a loan, despite my strong aversion to debt and owing, I fell for it . Against my better judgment, I reluctantly took out a loan to cover the program costs plus another program to do a 3day mentorship with them back in April, believing their promise that they would handle everything for me over the next three months.Their “done-for-you” service was a 3months collaboration supposed to include setting up my business (phase 1), finding the best locations for serviced accommodation, analyzing areas for you, and speaking to agents incase you were scared and more as described on the zoomI traveled to Essex for the three-day retreat, a costly trip given that I don’t live in England or Wales, I’ve never done this before in my life . But you know what they say “ you gotta step out of your comfort zone “ and to be frank I felt so proud of myself stepping out .During the retreat, I was pulled aside and pressured to join another VIP program for £30,000. Despite already being stretched financially, I vividly remember OLIVER, one of their team members, told me I was making a mistake by not upgrading. Their lack of empathy was shocking—here I was, someone who had just taken out a huge loan for the “do it for you service” spoken about, being told I was making a "wrong choice" by not going deeper into debt.Despite this , I had faith that the ‘do it for you ‘service will work out even if I was threatened it was the wrong choice if I don’t go for the VIP. I hoped the initial program would deliver, but it only got worse . I was assigned a mentor, Rebecca, and was told the initial business setup (including business cards and a website basically phase 1) would take two weeks. But meehhnnn did this phase 1 take months and months , from my point of view, I couldn’t start my business as I had a plan to advertise it using my cards and website obviously one would need something if you are willing to go out there and do the work or speak to people The mentorship was equally disappointing. Sessions were scheduled at their convenience, with no consideration for my availability. There were times when I had work and if you missed a session , there was no option to reschedule—it was simply gone and I wondered why would something that I paid for do it only at their convenience and their convenience alone, they simply did not care and if you missed it , you missed it but here I am , I waited for phase 1 that was promised two weeks , I waited months for that and I was suppose to accommodate that ??? No pity whatsoever. Communication was abysmal. Getting a response from my mentor often took weeks, sometimes over a month. Whenever I raised concerns,she would get back to me explaining she was “busy,” which left me feeling neglected and unsupported.I often had to rely on advice from others via TikTok or YouTube, despite paying for a dedicated mentor. I would go to other people for advice and they were available 24/7 . THAT THERE WAS HELP!!I respected the fact that I should do a few things myself obviously that was how one was suppose to learn but the lack of communication and support left me alone Even after voicing my concerns, nothing changed. The lack of communication and support has persisted, and I’m still trying to get my money back and it still continues . I DID NOT GET ANY ‘DO IT FOR YOU OR DO IT WITH YOU’ service . NOTHING WHATSOEVER. This is where it even hurts even more. I’m not based in England and wales and because of the laws of the country, I live in , nobody advised me it wasn’t right to do it there . Now on realization , the contract they provided me with does not even align causing me to redraft and pay for a new one , basically the serviced accommodation, everything they said was  suited only to England causing me to squander so much money in the process of getting a property .If you’re considering Asset For Life, think twice. My experience has been one of pressure, unmet promises, and poor support and it has left me in debt the one thing I forever hated and would not wish upon anyone Stay away from this scamming company I beg you, PLEASE

review: As an extended family we have previously enjoyed doing treasure trails together, but Ashbourne in Derbyshire was pretty much a disaster. It begins in a park, fine, but then there was an extremely dangerous road to cross followed by a long stretch along a shopping street with narrow pavement and continuous cars and motor bikes thundering past. It then moved on to a church which was better, but by then we were stressed and exhausted, and gave up. A great shame. I won't stop doing treasure trails on holiday but my advice would be go round them on street view first to check if the route is actually safe for a family.

We are here to help and advise you. Our aim is to discover which section of the industry you are best suited to and guide you on the road to success.

The studio bookings team will help and guide you into booking a test shoot if lucky enough to have been invited.
title: I was really nervous but the admin team…
review: I was really nervous but the admin team and advisers made me feel so confident that I was able to even go alone to my first photo shoot since I was 7. It’s been nearly 20 years that I’ve had a photo shoot for modelling!! I felt at home and I can really trust the advisers and they are only a phone call away. They put you at ease and are really lovely people. My photo shoot pictures came out amazing. I do recommend this team because they are really supportive in your goals and truly believe in you, I would say if your younger to come with someone just as support because it can be intense especially in front of a camera. But my wait was not very long and went quickly to find out my results and I also got referred to agencies after wards free of charge. The instructions in the email was precise and I got some offers from agencies which I am in talks with. I’m very happy I chose platinum models to help me get started and appreciate them for referring me to other agencies! Was actually a pleasant surprise lol

There are numerous errors in the study materials. Finally, the biggest downfall was two people who work at NTP: Kimbly Mackman and Kelly Moore. Kimbly was very rude and negative to me on the phone and told me "your chances of passing the course are slim". Kelly Moore is a tutor and when I booked a support session with her. She was very unfriendly, had to ask Mark for answers numerous times that she didn't know and refused to teach me any information, she just kept asking questions when I said I was confused and didn't know, then she said she's concerned about my level of knowledge. Basically didn't know how to teach and didn't know what she was trying to teach. Overall, I wouldn't recommend because of these two rude and unhelpful people. I accept that no test is  perfect and there might be 1 or  dud questions, but to then require a 100% pass rate is stupid, unfair and just plain wrong. I have nothing against people going on holiday, but going on holiday at your busiest time of the year??In three weeks of being with them, the instructor only managed to mark one past paper and I struggled to get an audience with her to help me through the second one! I have paid £540 and cannot say that I’m getting my money’s worth! The reason I’m writing this review is not because I have anything against NTP, no, it’s so that, 1) they (NTP) will address this issues of staff shortages at the crucial times of the year. review: Attended the Birmingham academy in June. After a week of the course jake the owner paid for a highly skilled hairdresser/barber trainer Tim come in from London who has years of industry experience. It was good to see how both trainers Aaron and Tim approached cuts differently but both came out with a high standard of cut. The facilities we good too, never working in a barber shop the academy gave you a real feel for what its like to work in a barber shop which make you even more keen to get in to the industry. The course is cheap but don't let that put you off, i researched courses all over the in both Scotland and England and nothing offer the same level of content. Would highly recommend!

I was very pleasantly surprised, everyone on the course was really friendly and the teachers (Chris and Aaron at the time) I had were excellent. Very friendly, passionate and made you feel comfortable. Definitely made some new friends! The course was very easy to understand, they went through things step by step and nothing was too much trouble. I met Jake (owner) one day of the course and he was also very pleasant. I’m really glad I went on this course, it helped me determine that barbering was the career I wanted to get into. I’ve since gone on to further my education because personally I want to become an assessor in the future. You don’t have to go down this route, you will become shop ready as long as you listen and put the graft in! Would highly recommend to anyone who wants to learn the fundamentals and gain confidence. For the price you can’t go wrong!

review: The agent, Luke Sullivan, made me feel at ease immediately and guided me through the different requirements for information that he would need to further my case.I am confident that I will get a positive outcome.Update 12th April 2024.Advised by CEL that I should inform my bank, which I did (I hadn't done this too date as I was embarrassed that I had been scammed for the first time). I assumed that this was a courtesty to inform them that CEL were acting on my behalf and to say that their letter was on the way.My bank called me a few days later, the letter had arrived and they were going to refund my loss in full. I was also told that i could then choose whether to pay CEL, or not to do so, since they had a Fiduciary Duty to act in my best interests and inform me that my bank may well refund me, thus saving me having to pay CEL their 25% fee.This, in these terms, did NOT happen. I challenged CEL but they dug their heels in and insisted that they had achieved the result and were due the fee that I had contracted to pay. I took legal advice from Which?, who said that I had a strong case and should go through the Legal Ombudsman service. We were about to leave on a 3-week holiday and I did not want this dragging on. I was offered a very small reduction in the fee and agreed to settle, just to stop the acrimonious email exchanges.Bottom Line - ALWAYS speak to your bank FIRST, if no joy, then engage a service such as CEL

title: A very disappointing experience
review: I've been a victim of crypto scam, so this has been a difficult time coming to terms with this.I felt the banks were little or no help, so decided to reach out to CEL Solicitors.I initially spoke with legal advisor Matt and found him to be very friendly and professional. After listening to my lengthy rundown of events, he carefully took down the details, explained the process and send me over info via email to complete. This is the 1st step in dealing with a very painful experience. I cant comment on how successful CES will be, but they certainly have excellent reviews, so I'm hopeful.However after dealing with CEL , namely the paralegal Johanna, I have a different view! Once I passed on all my information, it was then so difficult getting a response from her after weeks of waiting on them getting back.... she ignored all my calls and emails, and only replied when i ccd in her superiors, she just clearly wasn't interested.The outcome was disappointing also.....Their reviews showed they have Crypto scam experience in tracing assets lost through Crypto Currency via the blockchain to recover funds and had the in-depth knowledge to take on these scammers. However CEL clearly took on the easiest option and went straight to the bank with my case, and were not interested in the Crypto scammers. Result was the banks still refused to refund, so the FOS was involved, and I eventually had to settle for half my losses, minus their 30% cut. The bank had clearly lied in their reply to the FOS with their response, (I had evidence of this) which I tried to discuss with Johanna, but they were clearly not interested in pursuing further, so I had little choice but to accept their offer. I felt I did not get the service or the fight I was hoping for with the 30% cut they charged...I was warned about them from several of their previous customers, just wish I had listed to them, rather than all the fancy radios and internet ads.....very disappointing experience

title: I would give them zero stars if I…
review: I would give CEL Solicitors zero stars if I could. I have been advised by national advice groups that I have a strong case for disrepair. I have had a solicitor with 30 plus years experience look at my case and received a positive response to move forward. I sent in my details and enquired to assign my case. Was told to only provide photos. Rather odd because paperwork is fundamental. My matter is document orientated with more structural issues and they couldn't grasp this fact. They took my photos. I heard nothing for two weeks. I kept chasing up for updates, a number of times I received none. When I did get hold of someone, I was told that they cannot take my case on due to a notice I have received. This notice was deliberately made by an incompetent individual and contradicts findings that were made by a surveyor and a local authority officer. I have reports that don't match from authorities. The authorities have their own perogative. This fact has been completely ignored. That malpractice played a part.It seems I was duped into a time wasting exercise as they never intended to help me at all.  I have been advised about the different ways tenancies can end, including a method that is based on retaliation. I would advise anyone seeking a solicitor not to deal with boutique agencies. It appears the case workers I dealt with believe all cases are all cookie cutter, standard or text book with no nuisances. They are limited in assisting clients. No two cases are exactly the same. In law it doesn't work that way. If everyone played by the book, then solicitors wouldn't exist and that is what some of these case workers need to understand. That is the reason why attention to detail is vital. A skill they clearly lack. Wrong doing is wrong doing, no matter how much it is disguised. I saw a lack of competence and professionalism. With such an approach, where is the prospect of a justifiable outcome?Instead opt for a less boutique solicitors, where people don't judge you first hand and focus on details and facts in line with the law. Where no stone is left unturned. As a client, find legal representatives you can work alongside you and have integrity, so you can trust them with their legal expertise. That is the only way you can get justice.

review: I wrote a review on February 20, 2024, after having a call with the First Response Advisor from CEL. As in my previous review, the service provided by the First Response Advisor was good. They explained how they would assist me, which gave me a sense of hope during a time when I felt quite hopeless.My case number is FRD247311.001, and my case handler is Thomas Ali.Unfortunately, my case was unsuccessful, and I have not received any money back from Halifax. This has made me question whether CEL has the necessary expertise to achieve better outcomes than other providers.My case was failed because I did not inform or confirm to the bank the scammer's existence. At the time, I had no clear understanding of what a "scammer" was or meant. I believe both Halifax and CEL should have a much deeper understanding of common scam tactics, how scammers operate, and what constitutes a “scammer.” For example, scammers often instruct victims to avoid mentioning their existence. It surprised me that CEL accepted this as a valid reason for rejection, leading me to question their expertise in handling my case.While CEL publishes examples of their success stories, I can’t help but wonder about the number of cases that fail. title: UK Migration Lawyers experience
review: I sponsored a person who was born in South Africa but had a British father who was born and raised in the UK.  His parents were not married, thus because he was born in South Africa and not in the UK, his birth certificate did not have his British father on.  I paid the UK migration lawyers £1000 in March 2018, which they said that they could assist us with the process and that it would still be possible for this person I sponsored to get his British passport.  I advised that it was urgent and paid for DNA tests to be done (additional £380) to prove that the applicant was the offspring of his British father.  His father was very old and in an old age home and I advised that we were limited with time.  The UK lawyer was extremely unhelpful and gave no guidance whatsoever on the process and how to take the correct steps to ensure that the applicant got his UK passport.  I literally had to chase the lawyer to do her job.  Due to there being no guidance and help, many mistakes were made and I had to keep paying fees for these mistakes.  Eventually 3 years of dealing with these lawyers and getting absolutely no where, the applicants father passed away from old age and the DNA tests were never done.  He never got his British passport and UK migration lawyers refuse a refund, even though they assisted in no way.  It was such a stressful 3 years and it's upsetting because these people are trained and competent to help people get their passports but all they show is apathy towards you and give no assistance because money is more important to them.  Very disappointing and horrific experience with this company.

title: Ok to good but there isn't any better
review: The process to purchasing tickets is usually hassle free. Minimal to no glitches. Fast checkout and delivery of tickets. If you have any problems after the fact is where they lose stars. (if trustpilot had half stars I'd actually give them 3.5)For instance I bought tickets to Innervisions at Knockdown Center in NY May 17 2019. The ticket scanner said my tickets were already scanned. I'm the only one with the tickets so, not by me! I reached out to RA, told them what happened and asked for a refund, after a lot of back and forth they ultimately said they can't without the promoters authorization. womp womp. I don't know how this mistake happened but sucks I had to eat the costs ($80)Majority of the time I don't have issues. But this will happen once in a blue moon. About 2 other  times I can think of on tickets I got from friends. Anjunadeep at Avant Gardner July 13 2019 ($70) Zero presents Masquerade at 1896 April 6 2019 ($63) Not necessarily RA's fault (could be venue/promoter/door worker/scanner etc) but wish they had better policies that served the customer in these instances or somehow limit these errors from happening as I'd prefer 100% working tickets. While those instances angered me and they have room to improve, they overall beat out ticketfly, eventbrite and tixr. RA usually has lower fees and early bird prices so they get most of my money. Majority if not all of the events I go to use RA as their main platform. They also have an app which is nice to have. But it doesn't have a download button for the tickets so you have to sign in on a desktop if you need to send it to a friend. There is no option to transfer or send tickets to another account. Also, I would suggest never putting your ticket up for resale on RA. Your ticket will NOT sell unless RA has sold all of THEIR tickets first. which means your tickets will only go in queue when it is a sold out event. I learned the hard way.

title: Disappointed by RA unjustifiably raking in extra profits at the customer's expense
review: On the whole I enjoy using Resident Advisor but their reselling platform has an absurd rule: "Resale tickets will always be available at the final ticket tier price. The original ticket holder benefits from a refund, while the promoter receives any additional revenue."This means if, like me, you bought a ticket for £22 and the final tier price was £60, either RA or the event promoter will resell and pocket the difference. I hoped to resell my ticket to recover the costs, but the likelihood of someone else trying to buy my ticket at 3 times the price is very low. It's a really icky way to rip off customers and has put me off using them for ticket purchases in future. (Also - the fact that the ticket is more expensive and less accessible means less people will buy the resale tickets so the event will receive less income on food/drinks/merch etc than if the ticket sold at its original price. Aside from being disappointed, it really doesn't make business sense.)EDIT (in response to RA's response): I only wanted to be reimbursed the same amount as what I originally paid (minus a booking fee). RA makes the decision to re-sell the ticket at a higher price and either RA or the promoter pockets the difference. Fairness does not equate to re-selling a ticket at a much higher price than what it was bought for. This is exactly what ticket touts do. Tickets should be re-sold at the same amount as what was originally paid, minus the booking fee.

review: Great venue to host an event, there was plenty of space for our guests (approx 85 people) with many commenting how nice the venue was. Noa catered the event with canapés and provided drinks at their bar. It was a relaxed, casual atmosphere that worked well for our drinks event.

description: Santander Work Café is for customers and non-customers. It brings together a bank, co-working space and café experience in a single place.
title: Alas, no quiet area in the cafe
review: Santander implies that there is a quiet place to work in the basement, where the rules say that you should be silent, take phone calls outside, not to disturb others, etc. They also ask you to consume food only bought on the premises, i.e Noa's food. That amounts to about minimum ten pounds if you want to work there many hours per day. However, in the basement there also is some clothes provider shop called Noble Suitor. Today the door of this shop was constantly open into the quiet area where cafe customers were trying to work on their laptops. People, including friends of the man working at the shop coming and going constantly and chatting loudly, the man's small child talking loudly to his dad via Whatsapp on the loudspeaker... I approached a lady at Santander desk with this issue, but she was dismissive, saying that the man was renting the premises and Santander did not care. That means that the quiet area is not available in Noa's. At least I should be able to bring my own food then...

description: A one of a kind Restaurant, Shop and Hot Tub Showroom based in Bishop's Stortford, Hertfordshire.
title: Amazing food & a magical Father Christmas experience
review: I have visited Home & Eat since the day they opened. Their food has continued to get better throughout the years. Early on, I felt their salads were a little bland, however things have CHANGED! The salads now excite me, the Salmon Poke bowls out of this world, the roast dinner now ranks amongst the very best in Bishops Stortford and I'm also a big fan of the brunch options. Yes it can get cold in there during the winter temperatures, but this is because of the size and type of building. I have never come in winter to find the heaters off, but I do use my noddle and come in extra layers - I do not expect it to be cosy, it's just impossible in this type of building. But I have always found the staff to be friendly. Last year we visited at Christmas for the Father Christmas experience, this was the best Father Christmas experience by far that I have taken my 3 daughters too, I was super impressed with it and my daughter totally opened up and found it really magical. I also find it a great place to bring my dog and it's such a big place that if you are not a dog lover, you'll find plenty of spaces to sit away from any dogs.

The waitress told us there were no meals being served until 1pm, we were not asked to sit and wait and have a drink or anything and we got the impression we needed to leave. I used to love it there but it was not very welcoming at all. I never normally complain about anything but unfortunately this time i felt i had to say something. It will be a while before i go back there!

description: A one of a kind Restaurant, Shop and Hot Tub Showroom based in Bishop's Stortford, Hertfordshire.
title: Avoid
review: Absolutely disgusted. Agressive owner. Will never return. Having been a user of this restaurant for some years I have been tolerant of slow service as the staff do their best. Me and my partner went in for a meal, waited 20mins before being asked what we'd like to drink. By 45mins we were still yet to have consumed a single thing, and the staff just kept walking by ignoring any attempt for eye contact. After 55mins me and partner finally had enough and walked out (very slowly to which none of the staff reacted). As we reversed out of our parking space a large bald man runs up to the car and started banging on the side and exclaiming our food has just arrived. We stated politely that after 55mins without even been given our drinks we had had enough. He continued to be very aggressive which frightened my partner and stated he was the owner and would now have to pay for our food himself. I have never been so disgusted with any establishments performance and reaction to poor service. Anybody working in hospitality understands the importance of at least providing drinks on arrival to keep customers happy. I will never return to this establishment and put money into such an agressive mans pocket . and will actively advise all who enjoy a pleasant meal to do the same. If however you like being ignored, having sticky tables, dying of thirst, waiting in a cold barn and being  abused by an angry owner than this is your place.

description: A one of a kind Restaurant, Shop and Hot Tub Showroom based in Bishop's Stortford, Hertfordshire.
title: SHOCKING
review: I don't usually do reviews but we come here. So, I've been to Home and Eat three times now, and it just keeps getting worse. We moved nearby on January 4th, and I thought, "Cool, this place looks good." But, man, was I wrong.The staff, especially this lady named Jolie, are just plain useless. They don't care about customers at all. The food is a mess too - super greasy, and the place is so darn cold that the food gets cold even before it hits the table. Plus, they serve drinks after the food, making everything even worse.But here's the kicker: when we complained about freezing, they just shrugged it off, saying it's the way things are there. Apparently, the owner doesn't like the heater on. And get this - the lady chef came out, stared at us, and laughed along with the other lady. We were shivering, and they found it funny.I won't be going back there. Seriously, if you're thinking about it, don't bother. The place needs some serious fixing up, and the people there don't seem to care about anything but having a good laugh at customers' expense.

description: A one of a kind Restaurant, Shop and Hot Tub Showroom based in Bishop's Stortford, Hertfordshire.
title: Rapidly gone down hill, not the place it was!
review: I used to visit this restaurant regularly, food was always amazing and staff so helpful and friendly.  I visited at the weekend for the first time in probably three years and was beyond disappointed with the whole experience.  We had been seated for almost half an hour before anyone took our drinks order, despite flagging down a waiter after 15 mins.  It seemed the staff didn't want to catch our eye as it would mean they would have work to do.  We ordered two english breakfasts, they didn't have all the items available for this so offered to double up on other items, which the didn't!  They also forgot the sides we ordered.  The cherry on the cake was when the childrens pizza turned up... two of the smallest, dingiest slices of pizza i've ever seen (appeared to be from a budget pizza, which probably cost less than £1, then served up only two slices - probably 20p's worth of pizza) then charged us £6 for it, with a couple of sticks of carrot and pepper.  I wouldn't have given it to my dog.  Worst experience, so disappointing as it used to be a lovely place to dine.  I won't make that mistake again.

At first they tried to seat us right beside a huge speaker, perhaps they thought we could all sign and didn’t want to have a conversation.Found a quieter spot and began to look at the menus, there were only about three other groups at other tables so not very busy . The table was filthy and sticky and we were going to ask for it to be cleaned but decided to just leave. First impressions and all that.This place has gone down hill and I will never be returning.

description: A one of a kind Restaurant, Shop and Hot Tub Showroom based in Bishop's Stortford, Hertfordshire.
title: Sunday lunch - not.
review: Full disclosure: before the lockdowns I was number one fan at Home and Eat. Breakfast most days, weekend lunches. Loved the quirkiness and friendliness of the staff. Sadly, since opening up again it’s all changed for the worse. Yesterday was very probably the final straw. Having booked for a small family Sunday lunch, we arrived on time and were “welcomed” by a surly girly whose thought bubble (“I’d rather be anywhere but here right now”) was just a bit too obvious. There were plenty of young staff in there looking very smart in their shiny new uniforms, ostensibly “led” by a smiley, slightly older lady who was dashing around to no obvious purpose. A couple sitting nearby were waiting (very) patiently to pay, and we were simply ignored. For twenty five minutes. (I’m a geek, I counted). Impossible to attract even the merest eye contact with a staff member. Rule number one in hospitality: friendly welcome, drinks order within 5 minutes. It was 2 p.m. and not even busy as England were playing Croatia. After said twenty five minutes of being apparently completely invisible, we upped and left. Guys, you have a shiny new website and booking system, but this is absolutely pointless if you’re going to treat customers like this. I was a £2k a year customer, but won’t be coming back again. There are much friendlier and more welcoming places to eat out in Bishop’s Stortford right now. Sorry.

I wish it was available in more pubs locally, they literally offer fizzy drinks (am I 10?!) or AF lager (never been into lager). It feels like I’m treating myself to a nice drink, like a G & T, but it has its own distinctive kick. I planned on cutting down on alcohol, I was a social drinker but after surgery took so long to recover from even a couple of large wines,  but I’m now alcohol free and thriving thanks to Feragaia and the TryDry App. Thank you!

I really wanted to like it, but the search for an enjoyable booze free spirit must continue.    The service/delivery was fine, but I felt the need to post this review when I realised Feragaia are removing and blocking any non-positive comments under their facebook adverts... Which ain't very honest.Reply to the Reply:  Thanks for getting in touch Jamie.  There is no need for a refund, I bought your product - and you supplied it - so all is good there.  I just really didn't like it. (Btw, having no sugar or sweetener was agreat selling point for me - and I'm pretty sure a sweeter version would not have appealed to more).   The one star I gave is fair mirror of my experience though.    And by the way - someone blocked me from being able to post a comment under your adverts - and all I said was that I found the taste minging - even with mixers - nothing more negative than that.  On the day I did that several other people had said the same thing, the next day I was blocked from commenting and both my and other peoples 'negative' comments were definitely all gone - with the same positive comments I'd seen the day before still there.... - So someone is cleaning up the comments on your facebook posts.

We provide an Ear Health Check as part of every ear wax removal consultation. This will determine exactly what the problem is and what the next step should be. If you do need excessive ear wax removed your nurse specialist & the results of your check-up will help you choose the most suitable procedure.

We offer all forms of specialist wax removal, such as Microsuction, Irrigation & Instrumentation.

title: Everything felt very very rushed
review: Everything felt very very rushed. I was taken in slightly late to enable an older woman who’d arrived very early to be seen without waiting which is fine and the right thing to do.  I’m not sure if that’s the reason everything felt extremely rushed or if it’s just like that all the time but I felt like I was in and out and very hurried, I didn’t really take in much of what was being said as all the info was said a a rate of knots although there was a flow up email. It also felt really odd to be taken into the room as the other person was leaving it, my head went straight to wondering if the necessary cleaning had been done. I guess new equipment was used so it’s not an issue but it was a bit of an unnerving way to start off. Overall I don’t feel any difference at all which I understand can be the case with these procedures.
